method: Additive dictionary expansion and reviewed sense relations. Root-family siblings share a documented lexical base; overlapping compound memberships never merge families. No spelling-prefix or transitive synonym inference.
license: Dictionary excerpts from Wiktionary contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0; source editions and URLs are retained per entry.
translation: AZ/EN glosses machine-assisted unless marked edited. Source research does not certify every possible lexical sense.

families.method: AI-assisted structural and linguistic audit of explicit dictionary evidence; not a professional lexicographic review. Single-base derivational chains only; no synonym or antonym transitivity.

policy.membership: Source-backed single-base Azerbaijani affix derivations; exact lemmas retained, including infinitives. members includes compound leaves; core_members is the canonical derivation family.
policy.closure: Canonical root is reached only through directed single-parent derivation; family siblings may be exposed without asserting direct derivation or synonymy.
policy.compounds: Each compound leaf attaches to its documented component family without merging families. Never union groups because the same compound appears in two member lists.
policy.homographs: Multiple source etymologies are held unless individually disambiguated.
policy.inflection: Only current main-map headwords admitted; archived forms and aliases are excluded. All prior form-review holds and additional explicit case-derived constructions remain held.
policy.sense: Family relationship does not imply same meaning, sense, part of speech or valency.
policy.coverage: Evidence-limited audit of existing snapshots, not a complete etymological dictionary. Some real family members remain ungrouped because evidence is missing or ambiguous.

compound_leaves.head: alqı-satqı
compound_leaves.text:
Antonymous compound of alqı + satqı. Due to term being overrepresented, it is difficult to pinpoint the original source. For a similar case, see alış-veriş, ilanbalığı.
The term, which was previously attested as alğı-satqı, was later adapted to the colloquial language. The latest orthography dictionary does not include the original form.
Cognates
* Chuvash суту-илӳ (sut̬u-ilü, “commerce, trade”, literally “selling and buying”),
* Karachay-Balkar сатыу-алыу (satıu-alıu, “commerce, trade”, literally “selling and buying”),
* Kumyk сатыв-алыв (satıw-alıw, “commerce, trade”, literally “buying and buying”),
* Nogai сатув-алув (satuv-aluv, “commerce, trade”, literally “selling and buying”),
* Tatar сату-алу (satu-alu, “commerce, trade”, literally “selling and buying”),
* Turkish alım satım (“buying and selling”, literally “buying and selling”),
* Uyghur ئالدىـساتتى (aldi-satti, “commerce, trade”, literally “buying and selling”),
Compare
* Albanian shitblerje (“commerce, trade”, literally “selling and buying”),
* Burmese အရောင်းအဝယ် (a.raung:a.wai, “commerce, trade”, literally “selling and buying”),
* Central Kurdish كڕين و فرۆشتن (“commerce, trade”, literally “buying and selling”),
* Russian купля-продажа (kuplja-prodaža, “an instance of buying and selling”, literally “buying and selling”)

compound_leaves.head: alış-veriş
compound_leaves.text:
Antonymous compound of alış + veriş. Literally, "taking and giving".
Due to term being overrepresented, it is difficult to pinpoint the original source. For a similar case, see alqı-satqı, ilanbalığı.
Cognates
* Bashkir алыш-биреш (alış-beriş, “commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Crimean Tatar alış-veriş (“commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Gagauz alış-veriş (“commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Karaim алыш-бериш (“commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Kazakh алық-берiк (alıq-berik, “exchanging gifts”, literally “taking and giving”), алым-берім (alım-berim, “exchanging gifts”, literally “taking and giving”), алыс-беріс (alıs-beris, “(trade) relations”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Kumyk алыш-бериш (alış-beriş, “commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Krymchak алыш-верыш (“commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Kyrgyz алыш-бериш (alış-beriş, “commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Ottoman Turkish آلیش ویریش (“commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Salar alci-verci (“commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Southern Altai алыш-бериш (alïš-beriš, “commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Turkish alışveriş (“commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Turkmen alyş-beriş (“arbitrage”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Uzbek olish-berish (“commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”), oldi-berdi (“commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”)
Compare
* Armenian առևտուր (aṙewtur, “commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”), տուրևառ (turewaṙ, “commerce, trade”, literally “giving and taking”),
* Georgian აღებ-მიცემობა (aɣeb-micemoba, “commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Gujarati લેણદેણ (leṇdeṇ, “commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Hebrew מַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן (“negotiation”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Hindi आदान-प्रदान (ādān-pradān, “exchange”, literally “taking and giving”), Hindi लेन-देन (len-den, “commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Lezgi гун-къачун (gun-q̄ačun, “commerce, trade”, literally “giving and taking”),
* Magahi 𑂪𑂵𑂢⸱𑂠𑂵𑂢 (len⸱den, “commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Persian دادوستد (“commerce, trade”, literally “giving and taking”)
* Northern Kurdish danustan (“commerce, trade”, literally “giving and taking”)

compound_leaves.head: ilanbalığı
compound_leaves.text:
Izafet II compound of ilan (“snake”) + balıq (“fish”). Per Əhmədov, related to Persian مارماهی (mārmāhī /mârmâhi, “eel”, literally “snake fish”), although hardly has any ground, judging from Mongolian могой загас (mogoi zagas, “eel”, literally “snake fish”) and Buryat могой загаһан (mogoi zagahan, “eel”, literally “snake fish”). The term being overrepresented makes it difficult to pinpoint the original source. For a similar case, see alış-veriş, alqı-satqı.

* Bashkir йыланбалыҡ (yılanbalıq, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Chuvash ҫӗлен-пулӑ (śĕlen-p̬ulă, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Crimean Tatar yılan balığı (“eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Gagauz yılan balıı (“eel”, literally “snake fish”),

* Karakalpak jılan balıq (“eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Kazakh жыланбалық (jılanbalıq, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Kumyk йылан балыкъ (yılan balıq, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Nogai йылан балык (yılan balık, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Ottoman Turkish ییلان بالغی (yılan balığı, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Tatar еланбалык (yılanbalıq, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Turkish yılan balığı (“eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Turkmen ýylanbalyk (“eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Uyghur يىلانبېلىق (yilanbëliq, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Uzbek ilonbaliq (“eel”, literally “snake fish”)
Compare

* Abkhaz амаҭԥсыӡ (amatpsədz, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Armenian օձաձուկ (ōjajuk, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Buryat могой загаһан (mogoi zagahan, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Dargwa чIичIала бялихъ (čIičIala bəliq, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Central Kurdish مارماسی (marmasî, literally “snake fish”),
* Georgian გველთევზა (gveltevza, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Gilaki مار مائی (mâr mâ'i, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Ingush лихь-чкъаьра (liḥʳ-čqʼära, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* East Circassian блэбдзэжьей (blɛbdzɛźej, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Kalmyk моһа заһсн (moğa zağsn, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Lezgi илан гъед (ilan ġed, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Mazanderani مرمایی (marmâyi, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Mongolian могой загас (mogoi zagas, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Northern Kurdish marmasî (“eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Ossetian калмгӕсаг (kalmgæsag, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Persian مارماهی (mārmāhī /mârmâhi, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Talysh morımoy (“eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Tajik мормоҳӣ (mormohi, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Udi дизикӏчаьли (diziḳčäli, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),

lack of belonging to something, rootlessness

compound_leaves.head: qida borusu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of qida + boru.

compound_leaves.head: alçaq
compound_leaves.text: alçaq lists alçaqboy as a derived term. Lexical composition alçaq (low) + boy (stature) reviewed; compound is a leaf, never a bridge between bases.

compound_leaves.head: boyaqotu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of boyaq (“dye”) + ot (“herb”).

compound_leaves.head: boyunbağı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of boyun + bağ.

compound_leaves.head: boyunduruq
compound_leaves.text: From Proto-Turkic *bōńduruk (“yoke”). By surface analysis, izafet I compound of boyun + duruq. Cognate with Turkish boyunduruk, Kyrgyz моюнтурук (moyunturuk), Uzbek boʻyinturuq, etc.

evidence.head: boğulmaq
sense_glosses: to choke, to strangle, to suffocate
to refrain from expressing one's thoughts or feelings

evidence.head: boşalmaq
evidence.text:
From boş + -al.
The 2nd sense is a semantic loan from Turkish boşalmak.

evidence.head: boşluq
sense_glosses: space bar, space (gap between written characters)

compound_leaves.head: boşbeyin
compound_leaves.text: Compound of boş (“empty”) + beyin (“brain”).

compound_leaves.head: boşboğaz
compound_leaves.text: From boş (“empty”) + boğaz (“throat”)

compound_leaves.head: boşqab
compound_leaves.text: Compound of boş (“empty”) + qab (“dish”).

compound_leaves.head: halbuki
compound_leaves.text:
Analyzable as hal + bu + ki, literally 'the thing is that'.
Compare Persian حال آن که (hâl ân ke), Ottoman Turkish حالبوكه (halbuki).

compound_leaves.head: beşbucaqlı
compound_leaves.text: From beş (“five”) + bucaq (“angle”) + -lı.

compound_leaves.head: dördbucaq
compound_leaves.text: Compound of dörd + bucaq.

compound_leaves.head: düzbucaq
compound_leaves.text: düz + bucaq

compound_leaves.head: düzbucaqlı
compound_leaves.text: From düz + bucaq + -lı.

compound_leaves.head: itibucaqlı
compound_leaves.text: From iti (“pointed, acute”) + bucaq (“angle”) + -lı.

compound_leaves.head: ucsuz-bucaqsız
compound_leaves.text: From uc + bucaq + -sız.

compound_leaves.head: üçbucaq
compound_leaves.text: Compound of üç + bucaq.

compound_leaves.head: erməni budaq cümləsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of erməni (“Armenian”) + budaq cümlə (“subordinate clause”). Literally, “Armenian subordinate clause”.

compound_leaves.head: mübadilə buferi
compound_leaves.text: Calque of Russian бу́фер обме́на (búfer obména). Izafet II compound of mübadilə + bufer.

evidence.head: bulanmaq
sense_glosses: to become dull, torpid (e.g. of mind)
to become soiled, dirty, smeared, stained

evidence.head: bulaşmaq
sense_glosses: to become dirty, to soil oneself, to get stained
to ruin one's reputation by participating in dirty, dubious business

compound_leaves.head: ala-bula
compound_leaves.text: Compound of ala (“mixed-color”) + bula- (“to mix”).

evidence.head: buraxdırmaq
sense_glosses: to have released, to get out of jail

evidence.head: burğu
evidence.text: From bur- + -ğu. Cognate with Turkish burgu (“screw, auger”), Chagatai بورغو (burğu, “screw, drill, auger”), Kazakh бұрғы (burğı, “drill bit, auger”).
sense_glosses: willow twigs used for tying and weaving

compound_leaves.head: badımcanburun
compound_leaves.text: Compound of badımcan (“eggplant”) + burun (“nose”).

compound_leaves.head: buruntaq
compound_leaves.text: From burun (“nose”) + tax (“to attach, fasten”).

compound_leaves.head: gülburnu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of gül + burun.

compound_leaves.head: itburnu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of it (“dog”) + burun (“nose”). Cognate with Kyrgyz ит мурун (it murun).

compound_leaves.head: qarğaburnu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of qarğa + burun.

compound_leaves.head: qoyunburnu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of qoyun + burun.

compound_leaves.head: ördəkburun
compound_leaves.text: Izafet I compound of ördək (“duck”) + burun (“nose”). Calque of Russian утконо́с (utkonós). Compare Bashkir өйрәкморон (üyräkmurun, “platipus”).

compound_leaves.head: buxar gəmisi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of buxar (“steam”) + gəmi (“boat”).

compound_leaves.head: qoşabuynuz
compound_leaves.text: Compound of qoşa (“double”) + buynuz (“horn”).

compound_leaves.head: qoşabuynuzlu
compound_leaves.text: From qoşa + buynuz + -lu.

compound_leaves.head: təkbuynuz
compound_leaves.text: From tək + buynuz.

evidence.head: buyurtmaq
sense_glosses: to commission, to place an order for (something custom-made, tailored)

compound_leaves.head: buzdağı
compound_leaves.text:
Izafet II compound of buz + dağ. Calque of English iceberg.
Cognates
* Uzbek muztogʻ,
* Kazakh мұзтау (muztaw),
* Turkish buz dağı,
* Tatar боз тавы (boz tawı),
* Kyrgyz музтоо (muztoo),
* Uyghur مۇز تاغ (muz tagh),
* Crimean Tatar buzdağ,
* Turkmen buzdagy.

compound_leaves.head: xanımböcəyi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of xanım + böcək.

compound_leaves.head: şər-böhtan
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of şər + böhtan.

evidence.head: bölmə
sense_glosses: division (process of dividing a number by another)
section, division (each of the separate parts of something resulting from division)

evidence.head: bölüşmək
sense_glosses: to give part of what one has to somebody else to use or consume.

evidence.head: böyütmək
evidence.text: Equivalent to böyü- + -t. Ultimately a derivation from Proto-Common Turkic *bedü- (“to grow, increase”).

evidence.head: bükmə
sense_glosses: verbal noun of bükmək (“to wrap, to roll”)
A traditional Azerbaijani sweet pastry from the Quba region, typically made with a thin dough filled with nuts, sugar, and spices, folded into a crescent shape and baked.

compound_leaves.head: həddi-büluğ
compound_leaves.text: From Classical Persian حَدِّ بُلوغ (hadd-i bulūġ, literally “edge of the full age”), equivalent to hədd + büluğ.

evidence.head: bülövləmək
evidence.text: From bülöv + -lə. Diachronically, the word contains two suffixes -lə, one of which is no longer recognizable.

compound_leaves.head: ağzıbütöv
compound_leaves.text: From ağız (“mouth”) + bütöv (“whole, intact”).

evidence.head: bıçaqlamaq
sense_glosses: to knife (to use a knife to injure or kill by stabbing, slashing, or otherwise using the sharp edge of the knife as a weapon)

evidence.head: bıçaqlaşmaq
sense_glosses: to stab/knife one another, to have a knife fight

evidence.head: bıçaqçı
sense_glosses: knifesmith, bladesmith (a cutler who makes knives)

evidence.head: bəhanəçi
sense_glosses: excuse maker, a person who finds an excuse for everything

compound_leaves.head: güc-bəla
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of güc + bəla.

compound_leaves.head: bəlğəmgətirici
compound_leaves.text: From bəlğəm + gətir- + -ici.

evidence.head: bələdçi
sense_glosses: escort (an accompanying person in such a group)

compound_leaves.head: bazubənd
compound_leaves.text:
Borrowed from Persian بازوبند (bâzu-band).
Equivalent to bazu + bənd.

compound_leaves.head: taxtabənd
compound_leaves.text: From Persian تخته بندی (taxtebandi). Equivalent to taxta + bənd.

evidence.head: bənzəmək
evidence.text: From Proto-Turkic *beŋiŕ (“face; to be similar; open forestless place on a mountain slope”). Equivalent to bəniz + -ə.

compound_leaves.head: insanabənzər
compound_leaves.text: From insana (“human”, dative) + bənzər (“similar”).

compound_leaves.head: kəpənəyəbənzər
compound_leaves.text: From kəpənəyə (“butterfly”) (dative) + bənzər (“similar”).

compound_leaves.head: meymunabənzər
compound_leaves.text: From meymuna (“monkey”, dative) + bənzər (“similar”).

compound_leaves.head: bərabərtərəfli
compound_leaves.text: From bərabər + tərəf + -li.

compound_leaves.head: bərabəryanlı
compound_leaves.text: From bərabər + yan + -lı.

evidence.head: bəstəkar
evidence.text: From bəstə + -kar. Compare Turkish bestekâr, Uzbek bastakor.

compound_leaves.head: bəyyallısı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of bəy + yallı.

compound_leaves.head: meşəbəyi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of meşə + bəy.

compound_leaves.head: başbəzəyi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of baş + bəzək.

evidence.head: bəzənmək
sense_glosses: passive of bəzəmək; to adorn oneself

evidence.head: calaq
sense_glosses: graft (small shoot or scion of a tree inserted in another tree)
grafting (act, art, or process of inserting grafts)
something or someone that is extraneous, redundant; an irrelevant addition; someone who doesn't belong

evidence.head: camaşırxana
sense_glosses: laundry (a place or room where laundering is done)

compound_leaves.head: can həkimi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of can (“life”) + doctor (“həkim”).

compound_leaves.head: cansıxıcı
compound_leaves.text: From can + sıxıcı.

compound_leaves.head: ikicanlı
compound_leaves.text: From iki (“two”) + can (“life, soul, spirit”) + -lı.

evidence.head: canfəşanlıq
sense_glosses: extreme diligence, zeal (especially one that is out of place or merely ostensible, not sincere)

evidence.head: canlandırmaq
sense_glosses: to vivify, to enliven (make more lively, cheerful or interesting)

compound_leaves.head: hazırcavab
compound_leaves.text: From hazır + cavab.

evidence.head: cazibədar
evidence.text: From cazibə + -dar. Compare Ottoman Turkish جاذبهدار, Uzbek jozibador.

compound_leaves.head: çoxcildli
compound_leaves.text: From çox + cild + li.

evidence.head: cilovlamaq
sense_glosses: to bridle (to put a bridle on)

compound_leaves.head: cinayət hüququ
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of cinayət + hüquq.

compound_leaves.head: cinayət-prosessual hüququ
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of cinayət + prosesual + hüquq.

compound_leaves.head: cinsi azlıq
compound_leaves.text: From cinsi (“sexual”) + azlıq (“minority”).

compound_leaves.head: göy cismi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of göy + cisim.

compound_leaves.head: ağciyər
compound_leaves.text: From ağ (“white”) + ciyər (“lung”).

compound_leaves.head: qaraciyər
compound_leaves.text: From qara (“black”) + ciyər (“lung”).

evidence.head: cücərti
sense_glosses: sprout (a new growth on a plant, especially emerging from the ground)

compound_leaves.head: cümlə üzvü
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of cümlə (“sentence”) + üzv (“member”), Russian член предложе́ния (člen predložénija).

compound_leaves.head: cürbəcür
compound_leaves.text: From cür + -bə- + cür.

evidence.head: cütlük
sense_glosses: Symmetry of interactions under spatial inversion
A set with the property of having all of its elements belonging to one of two disjoint subsets, especially a set of integers split in subsets of even and odd elements
The classification of an element of a set with parity into one of the two sets.

compound_leaves.head: cındır bazarı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of cındır (“rag”) + bazar (“market”).

evidence.head: cəbhəçi
sense_glosses: member or activist of Azerbaijani Popular Front Party

evidence.head: cəftələmək
sense_glosses: to bolt (secure a door by locking or barring it)

evidence.head: cərimələmək
sense_glosses: to fine (to issue a fine as punishment)

evidence.head: cərimələnmək
sense_glosses: passive of cərimələmək; to receive a fine, to receive a ticket

evidence.head: cərrahiyyə
sense_glosses: surgery (the medical specialty related to the performance of surgical procedures)

evidence.head: cəzalandırmaq
evidence.text: From cəzalan- (“to be punished”) + -dır. Cognate with Turkish cezalandırmak.

evidence.head: cəzalanmaq
evidence.text: From cəza (“punishment”) + -lan. Cognate with Turkish cezalanmak.

compound_leaves.head: cəzaçəkmə müəssisəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of cəzaçəkmə (“serving the punishment”) + müəssisə (“facility”).

compound_leaves.head: ya da
compound_leaves.text: Morphologically ya (“either, or”) + da (“too, as well, also”). Cognate of Turkish ya da.

evidence.head: dabankeş
evidence.text: From daban + -keş. Coined by Azerbaijani writer Rəsul Rza.

compound_leaves.head: dikdaban
compound_leaves.text: Morphologically from dik + daban.

compound_leaves.head: dəvədabanı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of dəvə (“camel”) + dabanı (“heel”). Compare Kazakh түйетабан (tüyetaban, “bean-caper”).

compound_leaves.head: en dairəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of en + dairə.

compound_leaves.head: uzunluq dairəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of uzunluq + dairə.

compound_leaves.head: yarımdairə
compound_leaves.text: Compound of yarım + dairə.

compound_leaves.head: yarımdairəvi
compound_leaves.text: Compound of yarım (“half”) + dairəvi (“circular”).

evidence.head: dalaşmaq
evidence.text: From dala- (“bite”) + -ş. Cognate with Turkish dalaşmak. Compare to talischirmen (“I fight”) in the Codex Cumanicus.
sense_glosses: to scuffle, fight (to contend in physical conflict with each other)

evidence.head: dalğıc
evidence.text:
Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (dalġuc); equivalent to dal- (“to dive”) + -ğıc.
Cognate with Turkish dalgıç, compare Gagauz dalgıç.

compound_leaves.head: ürək-damar
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of ürək + damar.

evidence.head: danlaq
sense_glosses: reproach, reproof, rebuke (mild rebuke, or an implied criticism)

evidence.head: daraq
sense_glosses: a toothed implement for grooming the hair
a fleshy growth on the top of the head of some birds and reptiles; crest.
magazine (a chamber in or attachable to a firearm enabling multiple rounds of ammunition to be fed into the firearm)

compound_leaves.head: daraqbatmaz
compound_leaves.text: From daraq + bat- + -maz.

evidence.head: davamlı
sense_glosses: durable, resistant, strong, not easily worn out
strong, determined, unyielding (of people, their characters etc.)

compound_leaves.head: suyadavamlı
compound_leaves.text: From suya (“water”, dative) + davamlı (“resistant”).

evidence.head: davam etdirmək
evidence.text: From davam etmək (“to continue, go on”) + -dir.

compound_leaves.head: ailədaxili
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of ailə (“family”) + daxil (“inside”).

compound_leaves.head: kəllədaxili
compound_leaves.text: From kəllə + daxili.

evidence.head: dayanacaq
sense_glosses: subject future definite participle of dayanmaq

evidence.head: dayandırmaq
evidence.text: Morphologically dayanmaq (“to stand, to make a halt”) + -dır.
sense_glosses: causative of dayanmaq (“to stand; to stop”)

evidence.head: dayanmaq
evidence.text:
From daya- + -n. Cognate with
Turkish dayanmak (“to withstand, rest, lean, tolerate”),
Turkmen daýanmak (“to rest”),
Crimean Tatar tayanmaq (“to lean”) and Crimean Tatar dayanmaq (“to tolerate, bear”),
etc.

compound_leaves.head: dayıoğlu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of dayı (“maternal uncle”) + oğul (“son”).

compound_leaves.head: dayıqızı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of dayı (“maternal uncle”) + qız (“daughter”).

evidence.head: dağılış
sense_glosses: destruction, falling apart, collapse, becoming ruined

evidence.head: dağılışmaq
sense_glosses: to go away, to disperse (in different directions), to go each to his own place

evidence.head: daşlamaq
sense_glosses: to pave (to cover something with paving slabs)

evidence.head: daşlanmaq
sense_glosses: passive of daşlamaq (“to stone; to pave”)

evidence.head: daşlaşmaq
sense_glosses: to throw stones at one another

compound_leaves.head: başdaşı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of baş (“head”) + daş (“stone”).

compound_leaves.head: daş-qaş
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of daş + qaş.

compound_leaves.head: daşqalaq
compound_leaves.text: From daş (“stone”) + qalaq (“pile”).

compound_leaves.head: idman daşı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of idman + daş

compound_leaves.head: karandaş
compound_leaves.text: Borrowed from Russian каранда́ш (karandáš), from a Turkic language. Equivalent to qara + daş.

compound_leaves.head: sinə daşı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of sinə (“chest”) + daş (“stone”).

compound_leaves.head: tısbağa
compound_leaves.text:
From Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (taš-baqa), equivalent to daş (“stone”) + bağa (“turtle; earlier: frog”).
Cognates
Cognate with Turkish tosbağa, Chagatai [script needed] (taš-baqa),Uzbek toshbaqa, Bashkir ташбаҡа (taşbaqa), Kazakh тасбақа (tasbaqa), Tatar, Kyrgyz ташбака (taşbaka), Uzbek toshbaqa, Uyghur تاشپاقا (tashpaqa, “turtle, tortoise”).

evidence.head: daşqın
evidence.text: From daş- (“to overflow”) + -qın. See Bashkir ташҡын (taşqın) for cognates.
sense_glosses: flood (overflow of water from a lake or river)

evidence.head: daşınmaq
evidence.text: From daşımaq + -n. Cognate with Turkish taşınmak.

evidence.head: daşıyıcı
sense_glosses: a person or object that carries someone or something else
a person or other organism that has a genetic trait, mutation or infection liable to cause a disease, but displays no symptoms

compound_leaves.head: dil daşıyıcısı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of dil (“language”) + daşıyıcı (“carrier”). Calque of Russian носи́тель языка́ (nosítelʹ jazyká).

compound_leaves.head: fikrindən daşınmaq
compound_leaves.text: Compound of fikir (“mind”) + daşınmaq (“to give up”).

evidence.head: deyinmək
sense_glosses: to mutter, to talk to oneself
to grumble, to complain, to grouse (at), to snarl (at)

evidence.head: deyişmək
sense_glosses: to argue, to have a quarrel
to clash, to spar, to trade bars (in meykhana, rap, and ashiq tradition)

evidence.head: deşik
evidence.text: From deşmək + -ik, from Proto-Turkic *deĺ- (“to make holes”). Doublet of dəlik. Cognate with Turkish deşik, Turkmen deşik.

compound_leaves.head: dəlik-deşik
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of dəlik + deşik.

evidence.head: dibək
evidence.text: From dib (“bottom”) + -ək. Compare Ottoman Turkish دیبك, Turkish dibek.
sense_glosses: a small hole dug in the ground to beat wheat to separate it from chaff or to pound rough or unhusked rice.

evidence.head: didik
sense_glosses: tattered, torn up into shreds or strands

evidence.head: diksinmək
evidence.text: Morphologically dik (“steep, upright”) + -si + -in. Cognate with Turkish tiksinmek.
sense_glosses: to start, to startle, to flinch, to wince
To loathe, to be disgusted by, to revolt at

compound_leaves.head: dikbaş
compound_leaves.text: From dik + baş.

compound_leaves.head: dikdaban
compound_leaves.text: Morphologically from dik + daban.

compound_leaves.head: almandilli
compound_leaves.text: From alman + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: azərbaycandilli
compound_leaves.text: From Azərbaycan + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: dəridilli
compound_leaves.text: From dəri + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: ermənidilli
compound_leaves.text: From erməni (“Armenian”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: farsdilli
compound_leaves.text: From fars (“Persian”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: fransızdilli
compound_leaves.text: From fransız (“French”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: gürcüdilli
compound_leaves.text: From gürcü (“Georgian”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: ikidilli
compound_leaves.text: From iki (“two”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: ingilisdilli
compound_leaves.text: From ingilis (“English”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: irandilli
compound_leaves.text: From İran + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: irlanddilli
compound_leaves.text: From irland + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: ispandilli
compound_leaves.text: From ispan (“Spanish”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: italyandilli
compound_leaves.text: From italyan + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: kürddilli
compound_leaves.text: From kürd (“Kurdish”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: portuqaldilli
compound_leaves.text: From portuqal + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: qazaxdilli
compound_leaves.text: From qazax (“Kazakh”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: rusdilli
compound_leaves.text: From rus (“Russian”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: tacikdilli
compound_leaves.text: From tacik (“Tajik”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: talışdilli
compound_leaves.text: From talış (“Talysh”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: tatardilli
compound_leaves.text: From tatar (“Tatar”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: türkdilli
compound_leaves.text: From türk (“Turkish; Turkic”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: uyğurdilli
compound_leaves.text: From uyğur (“Uyghur”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: yapondilli
compound_leaves.text: From yapon (“Japanese”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: yunandilli
compound_leaves.text: From yunan (“Greek”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: çexdilli
compound_leaves.text: From çex + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: çeçendilli
compound_leaves.text: From çeçen (“Chechen”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: çindilli
compound_leaves.text: From Çin (“Chinese”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: çoxdilli
compound_leaves.text: From çox + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: özbəkdilli
compound_leaves.text: From özbək (“Uzbek”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: ərəbdilli
compound_leaves.text: From ərəb (“Arabic”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: diş məcunu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of diş (“tooth”) + məcun. The word məcun originally meant "delicious". It developed later the sense "delicious jam or spread" under the influence from the similar sense of semantic loan from Russian па́ста (pásta). The sense "toothpaste" was derived as a semantic parallel semantic loan from or a calque of Russian зубна́я па́ста (zubnája pásta). Alternatively, borrowed from Turkish diş macunu to replace the Russian calque diş pastası.

compound_leaves.head: gecə-gündüz
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of gecə (“night”) + gündüz (“day”)

compound_leaves.head: gecəbəgündüz
compound_leaves.text: From gecə (“night”) + -bə- + gündüz (“day”).

compound_leaves.head: gecəqondu
compound_leaves.text: From Turkish gecekondu. Equivalent to gecə + qonmaq + qondu.

compound_leaves.head: gecəquşu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of gecə (“night”) + quş (“bird”).

evidence.head: genişlik
sense_glosses: expanse (a wide stretch, usually of sea, sky, or land)
scope (the breadth, depth or reach of a subject)
scope (opportunity; broad range; degree of freedom)

evidence.head: genişlənmək
sense_glosses: to widen, broaden, to expand (become wider, broader)

compound_leaves.head: genişmiqyaslı
compound_leaves.text: From geniş (“broad, wide”) + miqyas (“scale”) + -lı.

compound_leaves.head: genişyarpaqlı
compound_leaves.text: From geniş + yarpaq + -lı.

evidence.head: geriləmək
sense_glosses: to move back, go back, go down
to retreat, decline, be in decline

compound_leaves.head: geriçəkilmə
compound_leaves.text: Univerbation of geri + çəkilmə.

evidence.head: gerçəkçi
evidence.text: From gerçək (“real”) + -çi (“-ist”). Cognate with Turkish gerçekçi.

evidence.head: gediş
sense_glosses: course (a normal or customary sequence of events)

evidence.head: gedərgi
sense_glosses: destined to leave; [one] who must inevitably go, not able to stay

evidence.head: getdikcə
sense_glosses: more and more, increasingly (especially with verbs like artmaq or çoxalmaq)

compound_leaves.head: gediş-gəliş
compound_leaves.text: Antonymous compound of gediş (“going”) + gəliş (“coming”).

evidence.head: geydirmə
sense_glosses: verbal noun of geydirmək (“to cloth someone”)

evidence.head: geydirmək
sense_glosses: [with accusative] to get (on), to haft (on), to stick, to pin, to spit

evidence.head: geyim
evidence.text:
From gey + -im.
Cognates
Cognate with Bashkir кейем (kiyim), Kumyk гийим (giyim), Kazakh киім (kiyim),Kyrgyz, Southern Altai and кийим (kiyim), Tatar кием (kiyem), Crimean Tatar and Uzbek kiyim (“clothing”), Turkish giyim, Turkmen geýim etc.

evidence.head: geyinmək
evidence.text: From geymək (“to put on; to wear”) + -in. Compare Turkish giyinmek.

compound_leaves.head: çimərlik geyimi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of çimərlik (“beach”) + geyimi (“cloth”).

compound_leaves.head: gicdıllaq
compound_leaves.text: From gic (“crazy, mad, stupid”) + dıllaq (“cunt”). Compare Azerbaijani ağıllıdıllaq and Azerbaijani maydıllaq.

compound_leaves.head: qaragilə
compound_leaves.text: From qara + gilə.

evidence.head: giriş
sense_glosses: introduction (an initial section of a book or article, which introduces the subject material)

evidence.head: girişmək
sense_glosses: to set about, to start doing (something)
to get involved with, entangled with

evidence.head: girəcək
sense_glosses: subject future definite participle of girmək

evidence.head: gizlənpaç
evidence.text: From gizlənmək (“to hide”) + -mac. Compare atlanbac (“leapfrog”) and Turkish saklambaç.

compound_leaves.head: gorbagor
compound_leaves.text: From gor (“grave”) + ba + gor.

compound_leaves.head: göbək ciyəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of göbək + ciyə.

compound_leaves.head: göbəkbağı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of göbək + bağ.

evidence.head: gömrükxana
evidence.text: From gömrük + -xana. Compare also Persian گمرک خانه (gomrok-xâne, “custom house”).

compound_leaves.head: gönüqalın
compound_leaves.text: gön + qalın

compound_leaves.head: qoşagörmə
compound_leaves.text: Compound of qoşa (“double”) + görmə (“seeing, vision”).

evidence.head: görünmək
evidence.text: From gör (“to see”) + -ün (“[passive suffix]”). Compare Turkish görünmek.

evidence.head: görüş
evidence.text: From görmək (“to see”) + -üş. Cognate with Turkish görüş, Crimean Tatar körüş (“view, opinion”).

evidence.head: görüşdürmək
sense_glosses: causative of görüşmək: to make someone meet someone; to arrange a meeting; to arrange for someone to meet someone else

compound_leaves.head: dünyagörüşü
compound_leaves.text: Ultimately calque of English worldview. Izafet II compound of dünya + görüş.

compound_leaves.head: güngörməz
compound_leaves.text: From gün (“sun”) + gör- (“to see”) + -məz.

evidence.head: əks-göstəriş
evidence.text: From əks- + göstəriş. Calque of Russian противопоказа́ние (protivopokazánije).

evidence.head: göstərici
sense_glosses: indicator, index (a sign; an indication; a token)
road-sign (usually in the form yol göstəricisi)

evidence.head: götəş
evidence.text: From göt + -əş. The function of the suffix is unclear here.

compound_leaves.head: göt-göt
compound_leaves.text: Reduplication of göt (“ass”).

compound_leaves.head: götlü-başlı
compound_leaves.text: From göt (“ass”) + -lü + baş (“head”) + -lı.

compound_leaves.head: yekəgöt
compound_leaves.text: From yekə + göt.

evidence.head: götürülmək
sense_glosses: passive of götürmək; to be taken, picked up, removed etc.
to break into a run (suddenly; unexpectedly)

compound_leaves.head: götür-qoy
compound_leaves.text: Imperative antonymous compound of götür- (“to take up”) + qoy- (“to put down”).

compound_leaves.head: gövhəri-laməkan
compound_leaves.text: Izafet compound of gövhər (“gem”) + laməkan (“placeless”), ultimately from Classical Persian گوهر and Arabic لامکان.

evidence.head: göyərmək
sense_glosses: to germinate (of a seed, to begin to grow, to sprout roots and leaves)

evidence.head: göyərti
evidence.text: From göyər- (“to become blue”; historically or dialectally: “to become green”) + -ti.
sense_glosses: greens; vegetables, edible grass (i. e. dill, parsley, etc.)

compound_leaves.head: göy cismi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of göy + cisim.

compound_leaves.head: göy qurşağı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of göy + qurşaq. Compare Turkish gökkuşağı, Crimean Tatar kök quşağı.

compound_leaves.head: göytürk
compound_leaves.text: göy + türk

evidence.head: güzgü
evidence.text: From Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (gözgü). Equivalent to göz + -gü. Cognate with Kyrgyz күзгү (küzgü, “mirror”).

compound_leaves.head: acgöz
compound_leaves.text: From ac (“hungry”) + göz (“eye”).

compound_leaves.head: alagöz
compound_leaves.text: From ala + göz.

compound_leaves.head: dargöz
compound_leaves.text: From dar (“narrow”) + göz (“eye”).

compound_leaves.head: dördgöz
compound_leaves.text: From dörd (“four”) + göz (“eyes”).

compound_leaves.head: göz qapağı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of göz + qapaq.

compound_leaves.head: göz yaşı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of göz + yaş.

compound_leaves.head: gözmuncuğu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of göz (“evil eye”) + muncuq (“bead”).

compound_leaves.head: gözüaçıq
compound_leaves.text: From göz (“eye”) + açıq (“open”).

compound_leaves.head: gözüdoymaz
compound_leaves.text: Compound of gözü (“their eyes”) + doymaz (“insatiable”).

compound_leaves.head: gözəyarı
compound_leaves.text: gözə + yarı

compound_leaves.head: qaragöz
compound_leaves.text: From qara + göz.

compound_leaves.head: yaşılgöz
compound_leaves.text: Compound of yaşıl + göz.

compound_leaves.head: üz-göz
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of üz + göz.

compound_leaves.head: şəhlagöz
compound_leaves.text: From şəhla + göz.

evidence.head: gözlənmək
sense_glosses: passive of gözləmək (“to wait, to expect”); to be awaited, to be expected

evidence.head: gözlətmək
sense_glosses: causative of gözləmək (“wait”): to make wait, to keep someone waiting

compound_leaves.head: güc-bəla
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of güc + bəla.

evidence.head: güdük
sense_glosses: a vantage point with a view of the surrounding area
a session of watching for an approaching enemy, police, etc.

evidence.head: güllələnmək
sense_glosses: passive of güllələmək (“to execute by shooting”)

evidence.head: gülgü
evidence.text:
Derived from Proto-Common Turkic *külgü. By surface analysis, gül- + -gü.
Cognates
* Kazakh күлкі (külki, “laugh, mockery”),
* Bashkir көлкө (külkü, “laughter; laughing stock”),
* Uzbek kulgi (“laughter”),
* Kyrgyz күлкү (külkü, “laughter”),
* Tatar көлке (kölke, “laughter”),
* Uyghur كۈلكە (külke, “laughter”),
* Karachay-Balkar кюлкю (külkü, “laughter”),
* Kumyk кюлкю (külkü, “laughter”),
* Nogai куьлки (külki, “laughter”),
* Turkmen gülki (“laughter”),
* Krymchak кӱлькы (“laughter”),
* Crimean Tatar külkü (“laughter”), külgü (“laughter”),
* Karakalpak kúlki (“laughter”),
* Southern Altai кӱлкӱ (külkü, “laughter”)

compound_leaves.head: gülərüz
compound_leaves.text: From gülər, a form of gülmək (“to smile”) + üz (“face”).

evidence.head: güney
sense_glosses: sunny side of a hill or a mountain, well-suited for cultivation

evidence.head: güneyli
sense_glosses: an Azerbaijani person from Iran, Iranian Azerbaijani

evidence.head: günsüz
sense_glosses: sunless (without the sun or sunshine; shaded; shadowed)

compound_leaves.head: birisigün
compound_leaves.text:
From birisi + gün.
Cognates
Compare Karachay-Balkar бюрсюкюн (bürsükün) /бюрсикюн (bürsikün), Kumyk бирисигюн (birisigün), Kazakh бүрсігүні (bürsigüni), Nogai бирсигуьн (birsigün), Kyrgyz бүрсүгүнү (bürsügünü), Southern Altai бирсӱӱн (birsüün), Karaim birisikün etc., some of which mean 'the day before yesterday' and some - 'the day after tomorrow'.

compound_leaves.head: gündönümü
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of gün + dönüm.

compound_leaves.head: gündəyməz
compound_leaves.text: From gün (“the sun”) + dəyməz (third-person singular future indefinite indicative negative of dəymək). Compare English where the sun don't shine.

compound_leaves.head: güngörməz
compound_leaves.text: From gün (“sun”) + gör- (“to see”) + -məz.

compound_leaves.head: günorta
compound_leaves.text: Izafet I compound of gün (“day”) + orta (“middle”). Compare Old Turkic 𐰚𐰇𐰤 𐰆𐰺𐱃𐰆𐰾𐰃 (kün ortusï, “midday”).

compound_leaves.head: günvurma
compound_leaves.text: Izafet I compound of gün + vurma.

compound_leaves.head: günün günorta çağı
compound_leaves.text: From gün (“day”) + günorta (“noon, midday”) + çağ (“time, period”), literally “the noon time of the day”.

compound_leaves.head: ikigünlük
compound_leaves.text: From iki (“two”) + gün (“day”) + -lük.

compound_leaves.head: əməkgün
compound_leaves.text: Izafet I compound of əmək + gün.

compound_leaves.head: əvəzgün
compound_leaves.text: Izafet I compound of əvəz + gün. Intended to displace the Russianism otqul.

compound_leaves.head: gecə-gündüz
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of gecə (“night”) + gündüz (“day”)

compound_leaves.head: gecəbəgündüz
compound_leaves.text: From gecə (“night”) + -bə- + gündüz (“day”).

evidence.head: gündəlik
evidence.text:
From gündə + -lik, literally "a day, per day".
Cognates
* Bashkir көндәлек (kündälik)
* Kazakh күнделік (kündelik)
* Kyrgyz күндөлүк (kündölük)
* Tatar көндәлек (köndälek)
* Turkmen gündelik
* Uyghur كۈندۈلۈك (kündülük)
* Uzbek kundalik

compound_leaves.head: günün günorta çağı
compound_leaves.text: From gün (“day”) + günorta (“noon, midday”) + çağ (“time, period”), literally “the noon time of the day”.

compound_leaves.head: gürcüdilli
compound_leaves.text: From gürcü (“Georgian”) + dilli.

evidence.head: güzəm
sense_glosses: wool shorn off the sheep in the autumn.

evidence.head: gələcək
sense_glosses: subject future definite participle of gəlmək

evidence.head: gələcəkçilik
evidence.text: From gələcəkçi (“futurist; futuristic”) + -lik (“-ness”). Compare Turkish gelecekçilik.

evidence.head: gətirmək
evidence.text: From Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (keltürmek), [script needed] (geltürmek). Equivalent to gəl- + -dir. Cognate with Turkish and Turkmen getirmek.

evidence.head: gətizdirmək
sense_glosses: to bring, to bring from outside or from abroad
to import, to buy abroad and bring home

compound_leaves.head: anadangəlmə
compound_leaves.text: From anadan + gəl- + -mə. Literally, “coming from mother”.

compound_leaves.head: ağızgələsi
compound_leaves.text: From ağız + gəl- + -əsi.

compound_leaves.head: bəlğəmgətirici
compound_leaves.text: From bəlğəm + gətir- + -ici.

compound_leaves.head: gediş-gəliş
compound_leaves.text: Antonymous compound of gediş (“going”) + gəliş (“coming”).

compound_leaves.head: gələn il
compound_leaves.text: Compound of gələn (“coming”) + il (“year”).

compound_leaves.head: buxar gəmisi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of buxar (“steam”) + gəmi (“boat”).

evidence.head: gəmirici
evidence.text: From gəmirmək (“to gnaw”) + -ici. Cognate with Turkish kemirici.

evidence.head: gənclik
sense_glosses: quality or state of being young

evidence.head: gərginlik
sense_glosses: the condition of being held in a state between two or more forces, which are acting in opposition to each other
a feeling of nervousness, excitement, or fear that is created in a movie, book, etc.; suspense

evidence.head: gəzdirmək
evidence.text: Morphologically gəzmək (“to walk”) + -dir. Cognate with Turkish gezdirmek (“to walk”)
sense_glosses: to walk, take out on a walk
to go around carrying something; to have something with oneself while not at home (often used with üstündə (“on/at oneself”))

evidence.head: gəzinti
sense_glosses: revelry, open-air merrymaking, outdoor fete; (popular) festival

evidence.head: gəzişmək
sense_glosses: to take a walk/stroll, to promenade

evidence.head: gəzəyən
evidence.text: From gəzmək + -əyən. Cognate with Turkish gezegen.
sense_glosses: one who likes to walk, to go for a walk, to stroll
sexually immoral, one who sleeps around or has a reputation of doing so; (especially of women) hussy

compound_leaves.head: habelə
compound_leaves.text: Univerbation of ha + belə (“such, so”).

evidence.head: hallandırmaq
sense_glosses: to decline (to inflect for case and number)

evidence.head: hallanmaq
sense_glosses: to be declined, to be inflected for case
to be mentioned in connection with something, to appear in some context (especially in negative contexts, such as scandals)

compound_leaves.head: halbuki
compound_leaves.text:
Analyzable as hal + bu + ki, literally 'the thing is that'.
Compare Persian حال آن که (hâl ân ke), Ottoman Turkish حالبوكه (halbuki).

compound_leaves.head: çağırış halı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of çağırış (“call, appeal”) + hal (“case”).

evidence.head: hansısa
sense_glosses: any (at least one; of at least one kind)
some (a certain, an unspecified or unknown)

compound_leaves.head: haqq-hesab
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of haqq + hesab.

compound_leaves.head: haqq-ədalət
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of haqq (“truth, right”) + ədalət (“justice”).

compound_leaves.head: əmək haqqı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of əmək (“labour”) + haqq (“payment”).

evidence.head: havadar
evidence.text: From Persian هوادار. Equivalent to hava + -dar.
sense_glosses: having a good weather and clean air

evidence.head: havadarlıq
sense_glosses: protection, defense (of someone); standing up (for someone); patronage; advocacy, intercession (on someone's behalf)

compound_leaves.head: hava limanı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of hava (“air”) + liman (“port”).

compound_leaves.head: hərbi hava qüvvələri
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of hərbi + hava + qüvvə.

compound_leaves.head: hazırcavab
compound_leaves.text: From hazır + cavab.

compound_leaves.head: çoxhecalı
compound_leaves.text: From çox (“many”) + heca (“syllable”) + -lı.

evidence.head: hesablamaq
sense_glosses: to count (to determine the number of (objects in a group))

compound_leaves.head: haqq-hesab
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of haqq + hesab.

compound_leaves.head: sikmətli
compound_leaves.text: Blend of sik (“dick”) + hikmətli (“wise”).

evidence.head: hirslənmək
sense_glosses: to be angry, be mad, to get enraged, infuriated, incensed

compound_leaves.head: hirsləndirmək
compound_leaves.text: From hirslən- + dir.

evidence.head: hissəcik
sense_glosses: A very small piece of matter, a fragment; especially, the smallest possible part of something
Any of various physical objects making up the constituent parts of an atom

compound_leaves.head: nitq hissəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of nitq + hissə. Ultimately, calque of Latin pars orationis.

compound_leaves.head: hoqqa
compound_leaves.text: From Arabic حُقَّة (ḥuqqa, “water pipe; cup of a juggler”). The non-archaic senses are a back-formation from hoqqabaz (“juggler, trickster”), via Persian حقه باز (“player at cups-and-balls; juggler; pick-pocket; plotter, impostor”).

compound_leaves.head: qeyri-hökümət təşkilatı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of qeyri-hökümət (“non-governmental”) + təşkilat (“organization”).

evidence.head: hörgü
evidence.text: From hör- (“to plate, to weave”) + -gü. Cognate with Turkish örgü, Gagauz örgü.

evidence.head: hörük
sense_glosses: a braided rope used for grazing livestock
wattle (a wall made of branches and twigs)
masonry (anything constructed of the materials used by masons, such as stone, brick, tiles, or the like)

evidence.head: hörmətli
sense_glosses: dear, esteemed (a polite way to start addressing somebody, especially in writing; followed by name or title.)

compound_leaves.head: özünəhörmət
compound_leaves.text: Compound of özünə + hörmət.

compound_leaves.head: birhüceyrəli
compound_leaves.text: From bir (“one”) + hüceyrə (“cell”) + -li.

compound_leaves.head: çoxhüceyrəli
compound_leaves.text: From çox (“many”) + hüceyrə (“cell”) + -li.

compound_leaves.head: hündürəçıxdı
compound_leaves.text: From hündür + -ə + çıx- + -dı.

evidence.head: hüquqi
sense_glosses: relating to the law or to lawyers
having its basis in the law
lawful; conforming to, or recognised by the laws of society

compound_leaves.head: ailə hüququ
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of ailə + hüquq.

compound_leaves.head: cinayət hüququ
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of cinayət + hüquq.

compound_leaves.head: cinayət-prosessual hüququ
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of cinayət + prosesual + hüquq.

compound_leaves.head: hüquq-mühafizə orqanları
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of hüquq + mühafizə + orqan. Calque of Russian правоохрани́тельные о́рганы (pravooxranítelʹnyje órgany).

compound_leaves.head: torpaq hüququ
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of torpaq + hüquq.

compound_leaves.head: birhədli
compound_leaves.text: From bir + hədd + -li. Calque of Russian одночле́н (odnočlén).

compound_leaves.head: həddi-büluğ
compound_leaves.text: From Classical Persian حَدِّ بُلوغ (hadd-i bulūġ, literally “edge of the full age”), equivalent to hədd + büluğ.

compound_leaves.head: çoxhədli
compound_leaves.text: From çox + hədd + -li.

evidence.head: hədələmək
sense_glosses: to threaten (to make a threat against someone; to use threats)

compound_leaves.head: həftəsonu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of həftə + son.

evidence.head: həlledici
sense_glosses: decisive (putting an end to contest or controversy; final; conclusive)

evidence.head: həllolunmaz
evidence.text: From həll olunmaq (“to be solved, to dissolve”) + -maz.
sense_glosses: unsolvable (a problem that cannot be solved)

evidence.head: hərşeyşünas
evidence.text: From hər şey (“everything”) + -şünas (“-logist”). Compare Turkish herbokolog.
sense_glosses: know-it-all, ultracrepidarian (a person who offers an opinion on everything, whether they know anything about it or not)

compound_leaves.head: hərbi dəniz qüvvələri
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of hərbi + dəniz + qüvvə.

compound_leaves.head: hərbi hava qüvvələri
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of hərbi + hava + qüvvə.

compound_leaves.head: hərdənbir
compound_leaves.text: Univerbation of hərdən + bir.

evidence.head: hərlənmək
sense_glosses: to spin, to whirl, to go round, to circle

compound_leaves.head: işığahəssas
compound_leaves.text: From işığa (“light”, dative) + həssas (“sensitive”).

compound_leaves.head: həyat yoldaşı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of həyat (“life”) + yoldaşı (“comrade, mate”).

compound_leaves.head: Əlahəzrət
compound_leaves.text: From əla + həzrət.

evidence.head: ianəçi
sense_glosses: donor (one who makes a financial donation, contribution)

evidence.head: ibrətli

compound_leaves.head: ilanbalığı
compound_leaves.text:
Izafet II compound of ilan (“snake”) + balıq (“fish”). Per Əhmədov, related to Persian مارماهی (mārmāhī /mârmâhi, “eel”, literally “snake fish”), although hardly has any ground, judging from Mongolian могой загас (mogoi zagas, “eel”, literally “snake fish”) and Buryat могой загаһан (mogoi zagahan, “eel”, literally “snake fish”). The term being overrepresented makes it difficult to pinpoint the original source. For a similar case, see alış-veriş, alqı-satqı.

* Tatar еланбалык (yılanbalıq, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Turkish yılan balığı (“eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Turkmen ýylanbalyk (“eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Uyghur يىلانبېلىق (yilanbëliq, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Uzbek ilonbaliq (“eel”, literally “snake fish”)
Compare

* Abkhaz амаҭԥсыӡ (amatpsədz, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Armenian օձաձուկ (ōjajuk, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Buryat могой загаһан (mogoi zagahan, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Dargwa чIичIала бялихъ (čIičIala bəliq, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Central Kurdish مارماسی (marmasî, literally “snake fish”),
* Georgian გველთევზა (gveltevza, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Gilaki مار مائی (mâr mâ'i, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Ingush лихь-чкъаьра (liḥʳ-čqʼära, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* East Circassian блэбдзэжьей (blɛbdzɛźej, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Kalmyk моһа заһсн (moğa zağsn, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Lezgi илан гъед (ilan ġed, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),

* Persian مارماهی (mārmāhī /mârmâhi, “eel”, literally “snake fish”),
* Talysh morımoy (“eel”, literally “snake fish”),

Calque of Russian обме́н веще́ств (obmén veščéstv).

compound_leaves.head: qaçaqmal
compound_leaves.text: From qaçaq + mal.

compound_leaves.head: xammal
compound_leaves.text: From xam + mal.

evidence.head: malalamaq
sense_glosses: to daub (render with stucco, to apply plaster)

compound_leaves.head: mamauşağı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of mama (“mother”) + uşaq (“child”).

evidence.head: maneçilik
sense_glosses: disturbance (the act of disturbing, being disturbed)

evidence.head: maraqcıl
evidence.text: From maraq + -cıl. Attested since at least 2004.

compound_leaves.head: masaüstü
compound_leaves.text: From masa + üst.

compound_leaves.head: yük maşını
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of yük (“load, cargo”) + maşın (“motor vehicle”)

evidence.head: medalçı
sense_glosses: medalist (someone who has received a medal)

compound_leaves.head: axtarış mexanizmi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of axtarış + mexanizm.

evidence.head: meyilli
sense_glosses: prone, inclined (having a tendency, preference, likelihood, or disposition)

compound_leaves.head: meymunabənzər
compound_leaves.text: From meymuna (“monkey”, dative) + bənzər (“similar”).

compound_leaves.head: meymunçiçəyi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of meymun + çiçək. Literally, "monkey pox".

compound_leaves.head: meyvə-tərəvəz
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of meyvə + tərəvəz.

compound_leaves.head: meşəbəyi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of meşə + bəy.

compound_leaves.head: millətlərarası
compound_leaves.text: From Izafet II compound of millətlər + ara.

compound_leaves.head: çoxmillətli
compound_leaves.text: From çox + millət + -li.

compound_leaves.head: zillət vəkili
compound_leaves.text: Blend of zillət (“ordeal, oppression”) + millət vəkili (“deputy, assemblyman”). By surface analysis, izafet II compound of zillət + vəkil.

compound_leaves.head: minillik
compound_leaves.text: From min + il + -lik.

compound_leaves.head: mina sahəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of mina (“mine”) + sahə (“field”).

evidence.head: mindirmək
sense_glosses: to put (on a train, in a car etc.), to mount (on a horseback etc.)

compound_leaves.head: genişmiqyaslı
compound_leaves.text: From geniş (“broad, wide”) + miqyas (“scale”) + -lı.

compound_leaves.head: irimiqyaslı
compound_leaves.text: From iri (“large”) + miqyas (“scale”) + -lı.

compound_leaves.head: mixi yazı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet I compound of mixi (“cuneiform”, adjective) + yazı (“writing”).

compound_leaves.head: gözmuncuğu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of göz (“evil eye”) + muncuq (“bead”).

compound_leaves.head: muğam üçlüyü
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of muğam (“mugham”) + üçlüyü (“trio”).

compound_leaves.head: maddələr mübadiləsi
compound_leaves.text:
From izafet II compound of maddə (“substance, matter”) + mübadilə (“exchange”).
Calque of Russian обме́н веще́ств (obmén veščéstv).

compound_leaves.head: mübadilə buferi
compound_leaves.text: Calque of Russian бу́фер обме́на (búfer obména). Izafet II compound of mübadilə + bufer.

compound_leaves.head: yarımmüdafiəçi
compound_leaves.text: From yarım + müdafiəçi. Calque of Russian полузащи́тник (poluzaščítnik).

compound_leaves.head: hüquq-mühafizə orqanları
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of hüquq + mühafizə + orqan. Calque of Russian правоохрани́тельные о́рганы (pravooxranítelʹnyje órgany).

evidence.head: muştuluq
evidence.text: From phonological nativization of müjdəlik, from müjdə + -lik.
sense_glosses: reward that one pays to a messenger of good news, such as sweets or a minor sum of money

evidence.head: müjdəçi
evidence.text: From müjdə (“good news”) + -çi. Doublet of muştuluqçu.

evidence.head: mürtədlik
sense_glosses: the state fo being a renegate

evidence.head: mütaliəli
sense_glosses: well-read (well informed and knowledgeable through having read extensively)

compound_leaves.head: videomüşahidə
compound_leaves.text: Izafet I compound of video + müşahidə.

evidence.head: müəllimlik
sense_glosses: the qualities or duties of a teacher; teacherhood; teaching job

compound_leaves.head: ali təhsil müəssisəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of ali təhsil (“higher learning”) + müəssisə (“facility”). Calque of Russian вы́сшее уче́бное заведе́ние (výsšeje učébnoje zavedénije).

compound_leaves.head: cəzaçəkmə müəssisəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of cəzaçəkmə (“serving the punishment”) + müəssisə (“facility”).

compound_leaves.head: azadlıqdan məhrumetmə
compound_leaves.text:
From azadlıq + məhrum + etmə, literally “deprivation of freedom”.
Calque of Russian лише́ние свобо́ды (lišénije svobódy).

evidence.head: mənimsəmək
evidence.text:
From mən + -imsə.
Compare Turkish benimsemek (“to adopt, embrace, appropriate”), which lacks the sense 'to digest food'; it may thus be a semantic loan from Russian усво́ить (usvóitʹ).
sense_glosses: to appropriate, embezzle; to claim or use something as property especially when it belongs to someone else
to master, to learn, digest, internalize, understand

compound_leaves.head: ikimənalı
compound_leaves.text: From iki (“two”) + məna (“sense, meaning”) + -lı. Calque of Russian двусмы́сленный (dvusmýslennyj).

compound_leaves.head: çoxmənalı
compound_leaves.text: From çox + məna + -lı.

evidence.head: məntiqli
sense_glosses: logical (reasonable; in agreement with the principles of logic)

compound_leaves.head: yanacaqdoldurma məntəqəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of yanacaqdoldurma (“refueling”) + məntəqə (“facility”).

compound_leaves.head: məqsədyönlü
compound_leaves.text: From məqsəd (“purpose”) + yön (“direction”) + -lü. Calque of Russian целенапра́вленный (celenaprávlennyj).

evidence.head: məqsədəuyğunluq
sense_glosses: reasonability, suitability (of chosen measures to intended ends)

evidence.head: məramnamə
sense_glosses: programme (set of goals stated by an organization, such as a lobby organization or political party)

compound_leaves.head: sülhməramlı
compound_leaves.text: From sülh (“peace”) + məram (“purpose, intent”) + lı.

evidence.head: namərd
evidence.text: From Persian نامرد, equivalent to na- + mərd.

compound_leaves.head: ticarət mərkəzi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of ticarət (“trade”) + mərkəz (“center”)

compound_leaves.head: çoxmərtəbə
compound_leaves.text: Compound of çox (“many”) + mərtəbə (“floor”).

compound_leaves.head: çoxmərtəbəli
compound_leaves.text: From çox (“many”) + mərtəbə (“floor”) + -li.

evidence.head: məskunlaşdırmaq
sense_glosses: to settle (to move people to a land or territory)

evidence.head: məskunlaşmaq
sense_glosses: to settle (to establish a dwelling place, home, or colony)

evidence.head: məsləhətləşmək
sense_glosses: to consult, to confer, to deliberate

compound_leaves.head: məsumluq
compound_leaves.text: From məsum (“innocent”) + -luq.

evidence.head: mətbəəçi
evidence.text: Morphologically mətbəə + -çi. Cognate with Turkish matbaacı.
sense_glosses: printer, operator of a printing press
printer, owner of a printing business

compound_leaves.head: özünəməxsus
compound_leaves.text: From özünə + məxsus.

evidence.head: məzəli
evidence.text: məzə + -li. Compare Uzbek mazali, Kumyk мазалы (mazalı), Turkmen mazaly.

evidence.head: binamus
evidence.text: From Persian بیناموس (bi-nâmus). Equivalent to bi- + namus.

evidence.head: namuslu
sense_glosses: honorable, honest, respectable; having his/her honor intact

compound_leaves.head: ürəyinazik
compound_leaves.text: From ürəyi (“heart-3sg.poss”) + nazik (“gentle”).

compound_leaves.head: baş nazir
compound_leaves.text: From baş (“head, main”) + nazir (“minister”).

evidence.head: nağaraxana
sense_glosses: a place where a wedding is held

evidence.head: naşükürlük
sense_glosses: ungratefulness, thankfulness; (especially towards providence; not appreciating what one has)

compound_leaves.head: neftayırma
compound_leaves.text: Izafet I compound of neft + ayırma.

compound_leaves.head: nehrə yağı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of nehrə + yağ.

evidence.head: neçənci
sense_glosses: what number, which (in a numbered series), whatth

compound_leaves.head: nida işarəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of nida (“exclamation, interjection”) + işarə (“sign”).

compound_leaves.head: nisyə dəftəri
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of nisyə + dəftər.

compound_leaves.head: nitq hissəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of nitq + hissə. Ultimately, calque of Latin pars orationis.

evidence.head: nizamlamaq
sense_glosses: to control or direct according to rule, principle, or law

evidence.head: nizamnamə
sense_glosses: association statutes, organization charter, bylaw (set of rules regulating the purpose and conduct of an organization)

compound_leaves.head: nizam-intizam
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of nizam + intizam.

compound_leaves.head: nəzər nöqtəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of nəzər + nöqtə.

compound_leaves.head: növbənöv
compound_leaves.text: From növ + -bə- + növ.

evidence.head: nümunəvi
sense_glosses: serving as a model or sample

compound_leaves.head: nüvə silahı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of nüvə + silah.

compound_leaves.head: ikinəfərlik
compound_leaves.text: From iki (“two”) + nəfər (“person”) + -lik.

compound_leaves.head: çoxnəfərli
compound_leaves.text: From çox (“many”) + nəfər (“person”) + -li.

evidence.head: nəfəslik
evidence.text: From nəfəs + -lik. A modern coinage intended to displace the Russianism фо́рточка (fórtočka) being in wide colloquial use.
sense_glosses: fortochka (a small ventilation window inside the frame of the main window)

compound_leaves.head: təngnəfəs
compound_leaves.text: From təng + nəfəs.

compound_leaves.head: təngnəfəslik
compound_leaves.text: From təng + nəfəs + -lik.

compound_leaves.head: nərdtaxta
compound_leaves.text: Izafet I compound of nərd (“backgammon”) + taxta (“board”). Compare Persian تخته نرد (taxte nard).

compound_leaves.head: rəhmətliyin nəvəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet III compound of rəhmətlik (“deceased”) + nəvə (“grandchild”), literally “the grandchild of a/the deceased one”.

compound_leaves.head: özünənəzarət
compound_leaves.text: From özünə + nəzarət.

compound_leaves.head: nəzər nöqtəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of nəzər + nöqtə.

evidence.head: nəğməkar
sense_glosses: glorifier, praiser (one who praises something, especially in songs or poetry)

compound_leaves.head: el-oba
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of el + oba.

evidence.head: ocaqlıq
sense_glosses: fire chamber, furnace, firebox (especially in a steam locomotive)

evidence.head: oduncaq
sense_glosses: wood (the substance making up the central part of the trunk and branches of a tree)
timber (trees in a forest regarded as a source of wood)

evidence.head: onuncu
evidence.text: Morphologically on + -uncu. Cognate with Kazakh оныншы (onınšı), Turkish onuncu, Turkmen onunjy.

compound_leaves.head: onillik
compound_leaves.text: From on + il + -lik.

compound_leaves.head: səksən
compound_leaves.text: Inherited from Proto-Turkic *sekiŕ ōn (“eighty”, literally “eight tens”). Equivalent to səkkiz (“eight”) + on (“ten”).

evidence.head: on beşinci
evidence.text: Morphologically on beş + -inci. Cognate with Turkish on beşinci.

evidence.head: on birinci
evidence.text: Morphologically on bir + -inci. Cognate with Turkish on birinci.

evidence.head: on dördüncü
evidence.text: Morphologically on dörd + -üncü. Cognate with Turkish on dördüncü.

evidence.head: on ikinci
evidence.text: Morphologically on iki + -inci. Cognate with Turkish on ikinci.

evidence.head: on üçüncü
evidence.text: Morphologically on üç + -üncü. Cognate with Turkish on üçüncü.

evidence.head: ortaq
evidence.text:
From orta + -q.
Cognate with Turkish ortak, Bashkir уртаҡ (ortaq), etc.

compound_leaves.head: damaqortası
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of damaq + orta. Calque of Russian средненёбный (srednenjóbnyj).

compound_leaves.head: dilortası
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of dil + orta. Calque of Russian среднеязычный (srednejazyčnyj).

compound_leaves.head: günorta
compound_leaves.text: Izafet I compound of gün (“day”) + orta (“middle”). Compare Old Turkic 𐰚𐰇𐰤 𐰆𐰺𐱃𐰆𐰾𐰃 (kün ortusï, “midday”).

compound_leaves.head: ortabab
compound_leaves.text: From orta + bab.

compound_leaves.head: ortadaqaldı
compound_leaves.text: From orta + qalmaq.

compound_leaves.head: ortaçaplı
compound_leaves.text: From orta + çap + lı.

evidence.head: otarmaq
sense_glosses: to graze (to tend cattle while grazing)

compound_leaves.head: boyaqotu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of boyaq (“dye”) + ot (“herb”).

compound_leaves.head: bəngotu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of bəng + ot.

compound_leaves.head: istiot
compound_leaves.text: From isti (“hot”) + ot (“grass”). Compare Turkish isot and Turkish ısıot.

compound_leaves.head: kəklikotu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of kəklik (“partridge”) + ot (“herb, grass”). Cognate with Ottoman Turkish ككلیك اوتی (keklik otu).

compound_leaves.head: otaq temperaturu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of otaq (“room”) + temperatur (“temperature”).

compound_leaves.head: qonaq otağı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of qonaq (“guest”) + otaq (“room”). Calque of Russian гости́ная (gostínaja).

compound_leaves.head: yataq otağı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of yataq (“bed”) + otaq (“room”)

compound_leaves.head: əl otağı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of əl (“hand”) + otaq (“room”)

evidence.head: oturacaq
sense_glosses: subject future definite participle of oturmaq

evidence.head: oturuş
sense_glosses: sitting posture; manner of sitting; the way someone sits

evidence.head: oturuşmaq
sense_glosses: to take root, to strike root, to catch on

compound_leaves.head: otuzdurmaq
compound_leaves.text: From otur- + uz + dur, with elision of /-ur-/.

evidence.head: ovlaq
evidence.text: Inherited from Proto-Turkic *āb-lag. Synchronically analysable as ov (“hunt”) + -laq. Compare Turkish avlak, Turkmen āwlag, Uzbek ovloq.
sense_glosses: area for hunting, area abundant with game

evidence.head: ovçu
evidence.text: Morphologically from ov (“hunt”) + -çu. Cognate with Turkish avcı, Uzbek ovchi, Old Turkic [script needed] (avčï, “hunter”).

evidence.head: ovuntu
sense_glosses: decayed matter, material formed by disintegration, decay, crushing

evidence.head: ovuq
sense_glosses: a boundary mark separating fields or other cultivated plots of land

evidence.head: ovsunlamaq
sense_glosses: to enchant, to bewitch, to cast a spell (on)
to charm, to spellbind, to fascinate

evidence.head: ovundurmaq
evidence.text: From ovunmaq + -dur. Compare Old Uyghur 𐽰𐽰𐽱𐽶𐾀𐽹𐽰𐽲 (ʾʾvytmʾq, “to console a child; to spoil a child”).

evidence.head: oxuma
sense_glosses: reading (the process of interpreting written language)

evidence.head: oxunuş
sense_glosses: reading (the process of interpreting written language)
reading (legislature: one of several stages a bill passes through before becoming law)

evidence.head: oxutmaq
sense_glosses: to provide an education, give an education, send to school

evidence.head: oxuşmaq
sense_glosses: to sing off, to have a sing-off

evidence.head: oynaq
sense_glosses: joint (any part of the body where two bones join)

evidence.head: oynatmaq
sense_glosses: to shake (move from side to side)

evidence.head: oynaş
evidence.text: From oyna- + -ş. Cognate with Kazakh ойнас (oynas, “lover, adultery”).

compound_leaves.head: çoxoyunçulu
compound_leaves.text: From çox (“many”) + oyunçu (“player”) + -lu.

evidence.head: oğraşlıq
sense_glosses: passiveness to or acceptance of perceived sexual looseness of female relatives; cf. cuckoldry

evidence.head: oğlaq
evidence.text:
From Proto-Turkic *oglak (“kid, yeanling”); equivalent to oğul + -aq.
Cognates
*Karakhanid [script needed] (oğlaq)
*Kazakh лақ (laq)
*Khakas оғлах (oğlax)
*Kyrgyz улак (ulak)
*Uyghur ئوغلاق (oghlaq)
*Uzbek uloq
*Southern Altai улак (ulak)
*Turkish oğlak

compound_leaves.head: bibioğlu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of bibi (“paternal aunt”) + oğul (“son”).

compound_leaves.head: dayıoğlu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of dayı (“maternal uncle”) + oğul (“son”).

compound_leaves.head: eloğlu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of el + oğul.

compound_leaves.head: oğul-uşaq
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of oğul + uşaq.

compound_leaves.head: xalaoğlu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of xala (“maternal aunt”) + oğul (“son”).

compound_leaves.head: əmioğlu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of əmi (“paternal uncle”) + oğul (“son”).

compound_leaves.head: çimərlik paltarı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of çimərlik (“beach”) + paltarı (“cloth”).

compound_leaves.head: şirin pambıq
compound_leaves.text: From şirin + pambıq. Literally, “sweet cotton”.

compound_leaves.head: papaqatdı
compound_leaves.text: Compound of papaq (“hat”) + atdı (“threw, droped”).

evidence.head: partlamaq
sense_glosses: to fire, to be opened (about a gun)
to be stuffed, to eat more than necessary
to hit the roof, to get extremely angry (with acığından, əsəbindən, qəzəbindən, hirsindən, etc.)
to burst from grief, bad news, or the excitement of impatience

evidence.head: partlatmaq
sense_glosses: to blow up (to become popular very quickly)

evidence.head: paylaşmaq
sense_glosses: to share; to divide or distribute among oneselves

evidence.head: pinəçilik
sense_glosses: cobblery (the skill or trade of mending shoes, as practised by a cobbler.)

compound_leaves.head: şanapipik
compound_leaves.text: From şana (“pitchfork; comb”) + pipik (“crest”). Compare also Tat şünəbəsər (“hoopoe”).

evidence.head: pisləmək
sense_glosses: to backbite, to run down, to vilify

compound_leaves.head: planetlərarası
compound_leaves.text: From Izafet II compound of planetlər + ara.

compound_leaves.head: portuqaldilli
compound_leaves.text: From portuqal + dilli.

evidence.head: poxlu
evidence.text:
From pox + -lu.
Cognate with Turkish boklu
sense_glosses: filled with faeces, full of shit; feculent, shitty; filthy

evidence.head: pozğun
sense_glosses: spoiled (having a selfish or greedy character due to pampering)

evidence.head: pullanmaq
sense_glosses: to become wealthy, to start having money

compound_leaves.head: pul kisəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of pul + kisə.

compound_leaves.head: pulqabı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of pul + qab.

compound_leaves.head: çörək pulu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of çörək (“bread”) + pul (“money”)

compound_leaves.head: pəncərəaltı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of pəncərə + alt. Calque of Russian подоко́нник (podokónnik)

evidence.head: pərdələmək
sense_glosses: to curtain (to hide, cover or separate as if by a curtain), to obscure, to obscurate

compound_leaves.head: tüstü pərdəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of tüstü + pərdə.

evidence.head: qabıq
evidence.text:
From Proto-Turkic *kāpuk (“bark; skin; shell”).
Analyzable as qab + ıq.

compound_leaves.head: ayaqqabı
compound_leaves.text:
Historically an izafet II compound of ayaq (“foot”) + qabı (“container, case”), but hardly perceived as such presently due to phonological developments: ayaq lost its secondary stress and /ɡ/ in qabı is devoiced to /k/, something that only happens word-internally. Furthermore, the nominative plural is normally ayaqqabılar, not ayaqqabları.
Cognate with Turkish ayakkabı and Crimean Tatar ayaqqap. Middle Armenian ոտնաման (otnaman) may be a Turkic calque.

compound_leaves.head: boşqab
compound_leaves.text: Compound of boş (“empty”) + qab (“dish”).

compound_leaves.head: duzqabı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of duz + qab.

compound_leaves.head: külqabı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of kül (“ash”) + qab (“vessel”).

compound_leaves.head: pulqabı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of pul + qab.

compound_leaves.head: qab-qaşıq
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of qab (“plate”) + qaşıq (“spoon”).

evidence.head: qablaşdırma
sense_glosses: verbal noun of qablaşdırmaq (“to pack, to wrap”)

compound_leaves.head: daşqalaq
compound_leaves.text: From daş (“stone”) + qalaq (“pile”).

compound_leaves.head: babadanqalma
compound_leaves.text: From babadan + qalma. Literally, “inherited from grandfather”.

compound_leaves.head: mat-məəttəl qalmaq
compound_leaves.text: From mat (“stunned, bewildered”) + məəttəl (“astonished, perplexed”) + qalmaq.

compound_leaves.head: ortadaqaldı
compound_leaves.text: From orta + qalmaq.

evidence.head: qalstuklu

compound_leaves.text: From başı + qapaz + -lı. Literally, “he/she has a slap on his/her head”.

evidence.text: Morphologically from qapmaq (“to snatch”) + -ış. From Proto-Turkic *kap- (“to snatch”). Cognate with Turkish kapışmak.

evidence.head: qarlı

compound_leaves.head: qar adam
compound_leaves.text: From qar (“snow”) + adam (“human" or "person”)

compound_leaves.head: qarquşu

compound_leaves.text: Borrowed from Russian каранда́ш (karandáš), from a Turkic language. Equivalent to qara + daş.

compound_leaves.head: qarabasma

compound_leaves.head: qarabatdaq

compound_leaves.head: qarabaşaq

compound_leaves.head: qaraciyər

compound_leaves.head: qaradinməz
compound_leaves.text: Compound of qara + dinməz.

compound_leaves.head: qaradərili

compound_leaves.head: qaraqınıq

evidence.text: Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish قرداش, قردآش (qardaš). Equivalent to qarın (“womb”) + -daş (“fellow, sharer”). Literally, “those who share the same womb”. Compare Turkish kardeş.

compound_leaves.text: From ac + qarına. Literally, “into a hungry stomach”. Compare Turkish aç karnına.

compound_leaves.head: bacı-qardaş
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of bacı (“sister”) + qardaş (“brother”).

compound_leaves.head: qaqa
compound_leaves.text: Reduplication of qardaş (“brother”), originating in child speak. Alternatively, onomatopoeic. Compare Turkmen kaka (“father; paternal grandfather”).

compound_leaves.head: qardaşqızı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of qardaş (“brother”) + qız (“daughter”).

compound_leaves.head: qarınqulu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of qarın (“stomach”) + qul (“slave”).

compound_leaves.head: qohum-qardaş

compound_leaves.head: yekəqarın
compound_leaves.text: From yekə (“large”) + qarın (“stomach”).

compound_leaves.head: qarşıdurma

compound_leaves.head: qarşısıalınmaz

evidence.head: qatıqlamaq

compound_leaves.head: qatırquyruğukimilər

evidence.head: qaxac

evidence.head: qaynaq

evidence.head: qaynar

hot (marked by intensity or vehemence; especially of passion or enthusiasm)
hot (always staffed and able to give immediate assistance)

compound_leaves.text: From əl (“hand”) + qayır- (“make”) + -ma.

compound_leaves.head: qazaxdilli

evidence.head: qaçağan

to miss (to fail to grasp an opportunity etc.)

evidence.head: qaçış

compound_leaves.head: mərkəzəqaçma

compound_leaves.head: qaçaqmal
compound_leaves.text: From qaçaq + mal.

compound_leaves.head: daş-qaş

compound_leaves.head: qab-qaşıq

evidence.head: qoçaq
evidence.text:

Cognate with Turkmen goçak, Turkish koçak, Kumyk къоччакъ (qoççaq), Karakalpak қошшақ.

compound_leaves.head: şorqoğalı

evidence.head: qüvvətli

evidence.text:
From qüvvət (“strength”) + -siz.

to be hurt, take offense; to have one’s feelings hurt or to be disappointed

compound_leaves.head: alqı-satqı
compound_leaves.text:
Antonymous compound of alqı + satqı. Due to term being overrepresented, it is difficult to pinpoint the original source. For a similar case, see alış-veriş, ilanbalığı.
The term, which was previously attested as alğı-satqı, was later adapted to the colloquial language. The latest orthography dictionary does not include the original form.
Cognates
* Chuvash суту-илӳ (sut̬u-ilü, “commerce, trade”, literally “selling and buying”),
* Karachay-Balkar сатыу-алыу (satıu-alıu, “commerce, trade”, literally “selling and buying”),
* Kumyk сатыв-алыв (satıw-alıw, “commerce, trade”, literally “buying and buying”),
* Nogai сатув-алув (satuv-aluv, “commerce, trade”, literally “selling and buying”),
* Tatar сату-алу (satu-alu, “commerce, trade”, literally “selling and buying”),
* Turkish alım satım (“buying and selling”, literally “buying and selling”),
* Uyghur ئالدىـساتتى (aldi-satti, “commerce, trade”, literally “buying and selling”),
Compare
* Albanian shitblerje (“commerce, trade”, literally “selling and buying”),
* Burmese အရောင်းအဝယ် (a.raung:a.wai, “commerce, trade”, literally “selling and buying”),
* Central Kurdish كڕين و فرۆشتن (“commerce, trade”, literally “buying and selling”),
* Russian купля-продажа (kuplja-prodaža, “an instance of buying and selling”, literally “buying and selling”)

compound_leaves.head: sağdış
compound_leaves.text:
Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰽𐰍𐰑𐰃𐰲 (s¹g¹d¹ič), Turkish sağdıç (“best man”), Kipchak [script needed] (sagtuč), Old Uyghur 𐽻𐽰𐽲𐽸𐽶𐽽 (sagdïč, “close friend, companion, young follower”). Etymologically sağ (“right side”) + tuş (“equal, opposite side”).
First part of the compound, sağ, originally meant "healthy, sound", as is reflected on the Old Uyghur cognate and the adjective senses of the Azerbaijani word (see Proto-Turkic *sag (“healthy”) for more.)

evidence.head: sürtmək
evidence.text:
From Proto-Turkic *sür(-t)- (“to rub, smear”). Equivalent to sür- + -t.
Cognates
Cognate with Old Uyghur [script needed] (sürt-, “to rub”), Karakhanid [script needed] (sürtmēk, “to smear, rub, polish, clean”), Turkish sürtmek (“to rub, polish”), Bashkir һөртөү (hürtüw, “to rub, delete, smear”), Chagatai [script needed] (sürtmek, “to rub”), Kazakh сүрту (sürtüw, “to wipe, rub off”), Khakas сӱртерге (sürterge, “to smear, spread, rub”), Kipchak [Arabic needed] (sürüt-, “to erase”), Kyrgyz сүртүү (sürtüü, “to rub, wipe”), Southern Altai сӱртӧр (sürtör, “to smear, spread”), Tatar сөртү (sörtü, “to wipe, smear”), Turkmen sürtmek (“to rub”), Uyghur سۈرتمەك (sürtmek, “to wipe, scrub”), Uzbek surtmoq (“to wipe, polish”).
sense_glosses: to grate (in cooking: to shred by rubbing)
to chafe (to fret and wear by rubbing)
to smear, spread, anoint, (to distribute in a thin layer)
