compound_leaves.head: alış-veriş
compound_leaves.text:
Antonymous compound of alış + veriş. Literally, "taking and giving".
Due to term being overrepresented, it is difficult to pinpoint the original source. For a similar case, see alqı-satqı, ilanbalığı.
Cognates
* Bashkir алыш-биреш (alış-beriş, “commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Crimean Tatar alış-veriş (“commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Gagauz alış-veriş (“commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Karaim алыш-бериш (“commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Kazakh алық-берiк (alıq-berik, “exchanging gifts”, literally “taking and giving”), алым-берім (alım-berim, “exchanging gifts”, literally “taking and giving”), алыс-беріс (alıs-beris, “(trade) relations”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Kumyk алыш-бериш (alış-beriş, “commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Krymchak алыш-верыш (“commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Kyrgyz алыш-бериш (alış-beriş, “commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Ottoman Turkish آلیش ویریش (“commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Salar alci-verci (“commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Southern Altai алыш-бериш (alïš-beriš, “commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Turkish alışveriş (“commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Turkmen alyş-beriş (“arbitrage”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Uzbek olish-berish (“commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”), oldi-berdi (“commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”)
Compare
* Armenian առևտուր (aṙewtur, “commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”), տուրևառ (turewaṙ, “commerce, trade”, literally “giving and taking”),
* Georgian აღებ-მიცემობა (aɣeb-micemoba, “commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Gujarati લેણદેણ (leṇdeṇ, “commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Hebrew מַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן (“negotiation”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Hindi आदान-प्रदान (ādān-pradān, “exchange”, literally “taking and giving”), Hindi लेन-देन (len-den, “commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Lezgi гун-къачун (gun-q̄ačun, “commerce, trade”, literally “giving and taking”),
* Magahi 𑂪𑂵𑂢⸱𑂠𑂵𑂢 (len⸱den, “commerce, trade”, literally “taking and giving”),
* Persian دادوستد (“commerce, trade”, literally “giving and taking”)
* Northern Kurdish danustan (“commerce, trade”, literally “giving and taking”)

compound_leaves.head: xalaoğlu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of xala (“maternal aunt”) + oğul (“son”).

compound_leaves.head: xalaqızı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of xala (“maternal aunt”) + qız (“daughter”).

evidence.head: xalça
evidence.text: Equivalent to xalı (“a (large) carpet”) + -ça (diminutive suffix). Cognate with Kumyk халча (xalça).

compound_leaves.head: xammal
compound_leaves.text: From xam + mal.

compound_leaves.head: xanımböcəyi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of xanım + böcək.

evidence.head: xatırlamaq
evidence.text: Equivalent to xatir (“memory”) + -lə. Compare Turkish hatırlamak.
sense_glosses: to mention (e.g. someone's name in a conversation)

evidence.head: xatırlatmaq
sense_glosses: to remind of, to be reminiscent of
to remind (to bring to the notice or consideration)

compound_leaves.head: xaç atası
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of xaç + ata. Calque of Russian крёстный оте́ц (krjóstnyj otéc)

evidence.head: xeyirli
sense_glosses: useful, helpful, good (having a practical or beneficial use)

compound_leaves.head: xeyir-dua
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of xeyir (“blessing, good”) + dua (“prayer”).

evidence.head: xilaskar
evidence.text: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish خلاصکار. Morphologically xilas + -kar. Cognate with Turkish halaskâr.

compound_leaves.head: kəndxuda
compound_leaves.text: Partial calque of Classical Persian کَدْخُدَا (kadxudā, “kadkhoda”), from kənd (“village”) + xuda (“master, lord”).

evidence.head: avtoxuliqan
sense_glosses: someone who drives in a dangerous way; someone who breaks road safety rules

evidence.head: avtoxuliqanlıq
sense_glosses: an act of driving in a dangerous way; an act of violating the road safety rules

evidence.head: xırdalamaq
sense_glosses: break down (to divide into parts to give more details)
to diminish, reduce something grand or significant to something petty or insignificant
to break (to divide money into smaller units)

evidence.head: xəbərçi
sense_glosses: tattletale (one who tattles (reports others' wrongdoings), often a child seeking attention)

compound_leaves.head: təmas xətti
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of təmas + xətt.

evidence.head: yalançı
evidence.text:
Morphologically yalan + -çı.
Cognates
Cognate with Kazakh жалғаншы (jalğanšı), Kyrgyz жалганчы (jalgancı), Tatar ялганчы (yalğançı), Turkish yalancı, Turkmen ýalançy, Uzbek yolgʻonchi, Uyghur يالغانچى (yalghanchi).

compound_leaves.head: bəyyallısı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of bəy + yallı.

evidence.head: yaltaqlanmaq
sense_glosses: to suck up [with dative ‘to’] (to adulate or flatter (someone) excessively, generally to obtain some personal benefit or favour)

compound_leaves.head: ayaqyalın
compound_leaves.text: From ayaq (“foot, leg”) + yalın (“bare”).

compound_leaves.head: yalınayaq
compound_leaves.text: Compound of yalın + ayaq.

compound_leaves.head: əliyalın
compound_leaves.text: From əl (“hand”) + yalın (“bare”).

evidence.head: yamanlamaq
sense_glosses: to speak ill of, to backbite, to run down, to vilify,

compound_leaves.head: yaman-yoz
compound_leaves.text:
From yaman (“bad”) + yoz. The latter part is a contraction of the now archaic yovuz~yavuz~yavız, from Proto-Turkic *yabïŕ.
Uncontracted form yaman-yovuz~yaman-yavız does exist, too.

compound_leaves.head: yanacaqdoldurma məntəqəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of yanacaqdoldurma (“refueling”) + məntəqə (“facility”).

compound_leaves.head: yanardağ
compound_leaves.text: From yanar + dağ.

evidence.head: yanaşma
evidence.text: From yanaş + -ma. The sense “set” is a semantic loan from Russian подхо́д (podxód).
sense_glosses: set (a certain amount of repetitions of a physical exercise)

evidence.head: yanacaq
sense_glosses: subject future definite participle of yanmaq

evidence.head: yandırmaq
sense_glosses: to set fire to, to light

evidence.head: yanğı
sense_glosses: occurrence of fire causing damage and danger

evidence.head: yanğın
evidence.text: Morphologically from yan + -ğın. Cognate with Turkish yangın, Turkmen ýangyn, Crimean Tatar yanğın, Uzbek yong'in, Tatar янгын (yanğın), Bashkir янғын (yanğın).

evidence.head: yanıq
sense_glosses: burn, scorch (a physical injury caused by heat or caustic chemicals)
only used in yanıq vermək and yanığını çıxmaq

compound_leaves.head: yanacaqdoldurma
compound_leaves.text: From yanacaq + doldurma.

compound_leaves.head: əlimyandı
compound_leaves.text: From əl + yanmaq. Literally, “[I] burned my hand”.

evidence.head: yanıltmac
evidence.text: From yanılt- + -mac. Cognate with Kyrgyz жаңылтмач (jaŋıltmac).

evidence.head: yanıltmaq
sense_glosses: causative of yanılmaq (“to err, to be mistaken”) : to mislead , to confuse, to deceive

compound_leaves.head: yapondilli
compound_leaves.text: From yapon (“Japanese”) + dilli.

evidence.head: superyapışqan
evidence.text: Partial calque of Russian суперклей (superklej), ultimately a genericized trademark held by Super Glue Corporation. By surface analysis, super- + yapışqan.

evidence.head: yapışdırmaq
evidence.text: Morphologically from yapışmaq (“to stick, intransitive”) + -dır. Cognate with Chuvash ҫыпӑҫтар (śyp̬ăśtar), etc.
sense_glosses: to stick (to attach with glue or as if by gluing)

evidence.head: yapışqan
evidence.text: From yapış + -qan. Cognate with Turkish yapışkan.

compound_leaves.head: qarayara
compound_leaves.text: From qara + yara.

evidence.head: yaraşmaq
sense_glosses: to be appropriate, become, be worthy of somebody
to be fit, to suit, look attractive on somebody

compound_leaves.head: yaraq-yasaq
compound_leaves.text: Synonymous compound of yaraq + yasaq, the latter part being a loan from Middle Mongol ᠵᠡᠪᠰᠡᠭ (ǰebseg), cognate with Khalkha Mongolian зэвсэг (zevseg, “weapon”); not related to Azerbaijani yasaq (“prohibition”).

compound_leaves.head: yaraq-əsbab
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of yaraq + əsbab.

compound_leaves.head: yaraq-əsləhə
compound_leaves.text: Synonymous compound of yaraq + əsləhə.

compound_leaves.head: əkinəyararlı
compound_leaves.text: Univerbation of əkinə + yararlı.

compound_leaves.head: əkinəyararsız
compound_leaves.text: Univerbation of əkinə + yararsız.

evidence.head: yaradılış
sense_glosses: all which exists; the universe, the world

evidence.head: yarım
evidence.text: From yar- (“split, cleave”) + -ım. Cognate to Proto-Turkic *yarïm.

evidence.head: yarış
evidence.text:
Morphologically, from yarmaq (“to chop, cut, cleave, crack”) + -ış.
Cognates
Cognate with Karakhanid یَرِیشْ (yarïš, “contest, competition”); Turkish yarış,
Crimean Tatar yarış,
Kazakh жарыс (jarıs, “contest, competition”),
Kyrgyz жарыш (jarış, “running contest; competition”),
Southern Altai јарыш (ǰarïš, “running contest; horse race”),
Turkmen ýaryş (“contest, competition”), Tatar and
Bashkir ярыш (yarış, “contest, competition”),
Khakas чарыс (çarıs, “running contest; horse race”),
Tuvan чарыш (çarış, “running contest; competition”),
Yakut сырыс- (sïrïs-, “to race each other”).

evidence.head: yarışmaq
sense_glosses: to compete, to contest, to emulate

compound_leaves.head: ala-yarımçıq
compound_leaves.text: From ala + yarımçıq.

compound_leaves.head: gecə yarısı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of gecə (“night”) + yarı (“half”).

compound_leaves.head: gözəyarı
compound_leaves.text: gözə + yarı

compound_leaves.head: yarıköçəri
compound_leaves.text: From yarı + köçəri.

compound_leaves.head: yarımasılı
compound_leaves.text: Compound of yarım (“half”) + asılı (“dependent”).

compound_leaves.head: yarımdairə
compound_leaves.text: Compound of yarım + dairə.

compound_leaves.head: yarımdairəvi
compound_leaves.text: Compound of yarım (“half”) + dairəvi (“circular”).

compound_leaves.head: yarımfabrikat
compound_leaves.text: From yarım + fabrikat. Calque of Russian полуфабрика́т (polufabrikát).

compound_leaves.head: yarımfinal
compound_leaves.text: From yarım + final.

compound_leaves.head: yarımfinalçı
compound_leaves.text: From yarım (“half”) + finalçı (“finalist”) or yarımfinal + -çı.

compound_leaves.head: yarımkeçirici
compound_leaves.text: From yarım (“half”) + keçirici (“conductive, conductor”).

compound_leaves.head: yarımkürə
compound_leaves.text: From yarım + kürə.

compound_leaves.head: yarımmüdafiəçi
compound_leaves.text: From yarım + müdafiəçi. Calque of Russian полузащи́тник (poluzaščítnik).

compound_leaves.head: yarımsavadlı
compound_leaves.text: From yarım (“half”) + savadlı (“literate”).

compound_leaves.head: yarımstansiya
compound_leaves.text: Compound of yarım (“half”) + stansiya (“station”).

compound_leaves.head: yarıyuxulu
compound_leaves.text: Compound of yarı (“half”) + yuxulu (“sleepy”).

compound_leaves.head: genişyarpaqlı
compound_leaves.text: From geniş + yarpaq + -lı.

evidence.head: yatıq
sense_glosses: sunken, pressed down or pressed flat

evidence.head: yatırmaq
sense_glosses: to top up, add (money, funds, credit)

evidence.head: yatızdırmaq
evidence.text: Morphologically from yat- (“to sleep”) + -ız + -dır. Two affixes with the same function have been used.

evidence.head: yavanlıq
sense_glosses: fatlessness, the quality of being without fat
dairy produce; bread spread or topping

compound_leaves.head: yavaş-yavaş
compound_leaves.text: Reduplication of yavaş (“slow”). Compare Turkish yavaş yavaş.

compound_leaves.head: əlbəyaxa
compound_leaves.text: From əl (“hand”) + -bə- + yaxa (“collar”).

compound_leaves.head: qarayaxma
compound_leaves.text: From qara + yaxma.

evidence.head: yaxınlıq
sense_glosses: sex, intercourse; sexual encounter or relationship

evidence.head: yaxşılıq
sense_glosses: favour, a kind or helpful deed; kind and helpful attitude; kindness

evidence.head: yayma
sense_glosses: rolling (process in which metal stock is passed through one or more pairs of rolls to reduce the thickness)

evidence.head: yayılma
sense_glosses: verbal noun of yayılmaq: spread, expansion, proliferation

evidence.head: yayındırmaq
sense_glosses: to distract, divert (requires possessed direct object)
to divert, to interrupt, to disturb

evidence.head: yayınmaq
sense_glosses: to deviate, digress (from a direction or topic)
to avoid, to dodge, to evade, to elude
to slip away, to sneak away
to hide, to get away from

evidence.head: yazdırmaq
sense_glosses: record (to make an audio or video recording)

evidence.head: yazı
sense_glosses: a text (such as a blog entry, a newspaper article or a column)

evidence.head: yazılmaq
sense_glosses: to sign up for, enroll, register for
subscribe (to sign up to have copies of a publication)

evidence.head: yazılış
sense_glosses: spelling (the manner of spelling of words; correct spelling or a specific spelling of a word)

evidence.head: yazışmaq
sense_glosses: to write to one another, to correspond

compound_leaves.head: mixi yazı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet I compound of mixi (“cuneiform”, adjective) + yazı (“writing”).

compound_leaves.head: səs yazısı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of səs (“voice, sound”) + yazı (“text, writing”). Calque of Russian звукозапись (zvukozapisʹ).

compound_leaves.head: yazı-pozu
compound_leaves.text: Antonymous compound of yazı + pozu.

compound_leaves.head: əlyazı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet I compound of əl (“hand”) + yazı (“writing”).

evidence.head: yağdırmaq
sense_glosses: causative of yağmaq (“to rain”); to make rain, to cause to rain
to unleash, direct, or send in large quantities

compound_leaves.head: nehrə yağı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of nehrə + yağ.

compound_leaves.head: sürtkü yağı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of sürtkü + oil (“lubrication”).

compound_leaves.head: azyaşlı
compound_leaves.text: From az (“little”) + yaşlı (“aged”).

evidence.head: yaşıllaşdırmaq
sense_glosses: to make (something) green, to turn (something) green
to add greenspaces to (a town, etc.)

compound_leaves.head: yaşılgöz
compound_leaves.text: Compound of yaşıl + göz.

evidence.head: yeddinci
evidence.text:
Morphologically yeddi + -inci. Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰘𐰃𐱅𐰨 (yetinči, “seventh”),
Turkish yedinci, Turkmen ýedinji, Kazakh жетінші (jetinši), etc.

compound_leaves.head: yekədöş
compound_leaves.text: From yekə + döş.

compound_leaves.head: yekəgöt
compound_leaves.text: From yekə + göt.

compound_leaves.head: yekəqarın
compound_leaves.text: From yekə (“large”) + qarın (“stomach”).

compound_leaves.head: səhər yeməyi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of səhər (“morning”) + yemək (“food”).

compound_leaves.head: yeniyetmə
compound_leaves.text: From yeni + yetmə.

compound_leaves.head: yeniçəri
compound_leaves.text: From Ottoman Turkish یڭیچری. Equivalent to yeni + çəri.

compound_leaves.head: yenidənqurma
compound_leaves.text: From yenidən + qurma.

evidence.head: yerli
sense_glosses: local (from or in a nearby location)

evidence.head: yerləşdirmək
sense_glosses: to be quarter, to house, to accommodate
to arrange a suitable accommodation for, especially lodging for the night
to be install, to set up (physically)

evidence.head: yerləşmək
sense_glosses: to be quartered, to be housed, to be accommodated

compound_leaves.head: dodaq yeri
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of dodaq (“lip”) + yeri (“place”). Literally, “place for lips”

compound_leaves.head: yer kürəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of yer + kürə.

compound_leaves.head: yeralma
compound_leaves.text: Izafet I compound of yer (“earth”) + alma (“apple”). Cognate with Turkmen ýeralma.

compound_leaves.head: yeraltı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of yer + alt.

compound_leaves.head: yerbəyer
compound_leaves.text: From yer + -bə- + yer.

compound_leaves.head: yerdəyişmə
compound_leaves.text: yer + dəyiş- + -mə.

compound_leaves.head: yerkökü
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of yer + kök.

compound_leaves.head: yerüstü
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of yer + üst.

compound_leaves.head: çoxyerli
compound_leaves.text: From çox (“many”) + yer (“place”) + -li.

evidence.head: yeritmək
sense_glosses: causative of yerimək (“to go”): to make go

evidence.head: yeriş
evidence.text:
Morphologically, from yeri- + -iş. Doublet of yürüş.
Cognates
* Bashkir йөрөш (yürüş, “walk”)
* Crimean Tatar yürüş (“walk; hike, march”),
* Gagauz örüyüş (“walk”),
* Karakalpak júris (“walk”),
* Kazakh жүріс (jüris, “motion, movement”),
* Krymchak йуруш (“gait”),
* Kyrgyz жүрүш (jürüş, “walk”),
* Kumyk юрюш (yurüş, “walk, gait, behaviour”),
* Nogai юрис (yuris, “walk”),
* Southern Altai јӱрӱш (ǰürüš, “walk”),
* Tatar йөреш (yöreş, “walk”),
* Turkish yeriş (“walk; fight, scuffle”) (Arpaçay, Kars; Erzurum), Turkish yürüyüş,
* Turkmen ýöriş (“walk”),
* Uyghur يۈرىش (yürish, “gate”),
* Uzbek yurish (“gate”)
sense_glosses: act of walking; manner of walking, walk, gait, step

evidence.head: yetirmək
sense_glosses: to deliver (an item or a message)
only used in özünü yetirmək to manage, to make it in time
only used in özünü yetirmək to rush, to hurry, to haste reaching some place
to keep pace, keep up (with a school subject)

evidence.head: yetişdirmək
sense_glosses: to grow, to raise, to cultivate
to breed, to rear, to raise
to train, to prepare, to form

evidence.head: yetişmək
sense_glosses: to come, to begin, to set in (of time)
to arrive in time (for), to be in time (for), to make it in time

compound_leaves.head: yeniyetmə
compound_leaves.text: From yeni + yetmə.

compound_leaves.head: yetərsay
compound_leaves.text: From yetər + say.

evidence.head: yoldaş
evidence.text: Morphologically yol (“road”) + -daş (“fellow, sharer”). Cognate with Kipchak یولداش (“travelling companion”).
sense_glosses: comrade (a fellow socialist, communist or other similarly politically aligned person)
comrade (A non-hierarchical title, functionally similar to "Mr.", "Mrs.", "Miss", "Ms." etc, in a communist, socialist, or rarely in an Islamist state.)
husband or wife (shortening of həyat yoldaşı)

evidence.head: yoluxmaq
sense_glosses: to come to see, to call (on), to visit
to catch, to contract, to be infected with

evidence.head: yolçuluq
sense_glosses: mendicancy (depending on alms for a living)

compound_leaves.head: ayaqyolu
compound_leaves.text:
Izafet II compound of ayaq (“foot, leg”) + yol (“way, path”). Cognate with Turkish ayakyolu,
Turkmen aýakýolu,
Crimean Tatar ayaqyol.

compound_leaves.head: dəmiryol
compound_leaves.text: Izafet I compound of dəmir (“iron”) + yol (“way, road”)

compound_leaves.head: həyat yoldaşı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of həyat (“life”) + yoldaşı (“comrade, mate”).

compound_leaves.head: iş yoldaşı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of iş (“work”) + yoldaş (“comrade, mate”) + -i (suffix used with compound nouns)

compound_leaves.head: yolverilməz
compound_leaves.text: From yol + ver- + -il + -məz.

compound_leaves.head: yorğanağı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of yorğan + ağ.

evidence.head: yoxalmaq
evidence.text:
From yox + -al.
Cognates
* Kazakh жоғалу (joğaluw, “to get lost”)
* Kyrgyz жоголуу (jogoluu, “to disappear, to get lost”)
* Uzbek yoʻqolmoq (“get lost”)
* Uyghur يوقالماق (yoqalmaq, “to get lost, disappear”)
* Turkish yoğalmak (“to disappear”)
* Turkmen ýogalmak (“to disappear, die”)
sense_glosses: to disappear, to vanish, to perish

evidence.head: yoxsul
sense_glosses: poor (with little or no possessions or money)

evidence.head: yoxsullaşmaq
sense_glosses: to become impoverished, to grow poor

compound_leaves.head: var-yox
compound_leaves.text: Antonymous compound of var + yox.

evidence.head: yoğurt
evidence.text:
Inherited from Proto-Turkic *yogrut (“curdled, coagulated milk”), from *yogur- (“to knead, to fluff up, to condense”) *-ut. Equivalent to yoğur- (“to knead”) + -d.
cognates
Cognate with Old Uyghur 𐽶𐽳𐽲𐽾𐽳𐾀 (yogrut, “yogurt”), Turkish yoğurt, Kyrgyz жуурат (juurat), and Yakut суорат (suorat).

evidence.head: yumurtalıq
sense_glosses: ovary (the lower part of a pistil or carpel that bears ovules and ripens into fruit)

compound_leaves.head: ürəyiyumşaq
compound_leaves.text: From ürəyi (“heart-3sg.poss”) + yumşaq (“soft”).

compound_leaves.head: yunandilli
compound_leaves.text: From yunan (“Greek”) + dilli.

evidence.head: yuvacıq
evidence.text: From yuva + -cıq. The sense 'outlet' is a partial calque of Russian гнездо́ (gnezdó, “nest; wall socket”).

compound_leaves.head: taxıc yuvası
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of taxıc (“plug”) + yuvası (“nest”).

compound_leaves.head: ürəyiyuxa
compound_leaves.text: From ürəyi (“heart-3sg.poss”) + yuxa (“soft, tender”).

evidence.head: yuxucul
sense_glosses: prone to sleep, loving to sleep a lot

compound_leaves.head: qarayuxu
compound_leaves.text: From qara (“black”) + yuxu (“sleep”).

compound_leaves.head: yarıyuxulu
compound_leaves.text: Compound of yarı (“half”) + yuxulu (“sleepy”).

evidence.head: yöndəm
sense_glosses: order (the state of being well arranged)

evidence.head: yönlü
evidence.text:
From yön + -lü.
Cognates
* Bashkir юнле (yonli, “sensible; decent; worthy, suitable”)
* Karakalpak jónli (“worthwhile, decent; right, fair”)
* Tatar юньле (yünle, “decent, honest; smart, intelligent; good, worthy, suitable”)
* Turkish yönlü (“suitable, good, correct, appropriate”) (dialectal, Burdur, Sivas, Niğde, Konya, Antalya)

evidence.head: yönəlmək
sense_glosses: to direct oneself (towards someone or something); to be directed towards
to head, to make one's way (intransitive)

evidence.head: yönəltmək
sense_glosses: to direct someone or something (towards someone or something else)

compound_leaves.head: məqsədyönlü
compound_leaves.text: From məqsəd (“purpose”) + yön (“direction”) + -lü. Calque of Russian целенапра́вленный (celenaprávlennyj).

compound_leaves.head: yan-yörə
compound_leaves.text: From yan + yörə.

compound_leaves.head: yük maşını
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of yük (“load, cargo”) + maşın (“motor vehicle”)

compound_leaves.head: taleyüklü
compound_leaves.text: From tale (“fate”) + yüklü (“loaded”).

compound_leaves.head: yüksəktezlikli
compound_leaves.text: From yüksək (“high”) + tezlik (“frequency”) + -li.

compound_leaves.head: yüksəkvəzifəli
compound_leaves.text: From yüksək + vəzifəli.

evidence.head: yüksəliş
sense_glosses: rise (the process of or an action or instance of coming to prominence)

evidence.head: yüksəltmək
sense_glosses: to praise, to glorify, to make famous (to give praise or glory to smb.)

evidence.head: yüngülvari
sense_glosses: light, slight (gentle or weak, not aggressive or powerful)
mild (not overly felt or seriously intended)

evidence.head: yürütmək
sense_glosses: causative of yürümək (“to go”): to make go

evidence.head: yürüş
sense_glosses: mileage, kilometrage (total distance covered in some time)

evidence.head: yüyənləmək
sense_glosses: to subdue, to control, to curb, to bridle

compound_leaves.head: yüzillik
compound_leaves.text: From yüz + il + -lik. Compare Kyrgyz жүзжылдык (jüzjıldık).

evidence.head: yığma
evidence.text: From yığ + -ma. The sense “national sports team” is a semantic loan from Russian сбо́рная (sbórnaja).
sense_glosses: verbal noun of yığmaq (“to gather, collect”)

evidence.head: yığım
sense_glosses: set, kit, outfit, collection (collection of various objects for a particular purpose, such as a set of tools)
harvest (process of gathering the ripened crop)

evidence.head: yığın
evidence.text: From yığ- + -ın, ultimately from Proto-Turkic *yïgïn (“heap, pile”).

evidence.head: yığışmaq
sense_glosses: to gather one's belongings; to get ready to go; to make oneself ready to leave

evidence.head: yəhərləmək
sense_glosses: to put a saddle on (an animal)
to control or restrain (someone or something), as if using a saddle; to bridle, to harness, to rein in

compound_leaves.head: yəhər-qayış
compound_leaves.text: From Dvandva compound of yəhər + qayış.

evidence.head: zehni
sense_glosses: intellectual (pertaining to, or performed by, the intellect; mental or cognitive)

compound_leaves.head: zillət vəkili
compound_leaves.text: Blend of zillət (“ordeal, oppression”) + millət vəkili (“deputy, assemblyman”). By surface analysis, izafet II compound of zillət + vəkil.

evidence.head: ziyanlı
evidence.text: Morphologically ziyan + lı. Cognate with Turkmen zyýanly, Uzbek ziyonli.

evidence.head: ziyansız
evidence.text: Morphologically ziyan + -sız. Cognate with Turkmen zyýansyz, Uzbek ziyonsiz.

evidence.head: ziyarətgah
sense_glosses: pilgrimage site, place of pilgrimage (e.g. tomb of a saint)

compound_leaves.head: zurnalist
compound_leaves.text: Blend of zurna (“a wind instrument”) + jurnalist (“journalist”).

evidence.head: zəhmətkeş
evidence.text: Borrowed from Persian زحمتکش (zahmatkeš), equivalent to zəhmət (“labour; effort; suffering; troubles”) + -keş.

compound_leaves.head: qida zəhərlənməsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of qida + zəhərlənmə.

compound_leaves.head: qida zənciri
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of qida + zəncir.

evidence.head: zəngləşmək
sense_glosses: to call each other, to contact someone by telephone

compound_leaves.head: künc zərbəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of künc + zərbə.

evidence.head: zərərsizləşdirmək
sense_glosses: to render harmless, disarm, defuse (a bomb)

evidence.head: zərərsizləşmək
sense_glosses: to be rendered harmless, to be disarmed, to be defused (a bomb)

compound_leaves.head: çindilli
compound_leaves.text: From Çin (“Chinese”) + dilli.

evidence.head: çalğıçı
sense_glosses: musician, instrumentalist (especially one who plays folk tunes on traditional instruments at weddings etc.)

evidence.head: çapacaq
sense_glosses: meat cleaver, butcher's cleaver, meat axe

evidence.head: çapalamaq
sense_glosses: to toss, to toss about, to writhe

evidence.head: çapovul
evidence.text: From çap- + -ovul. Cognate with Turkish çapul, çapavul, Uzbek chopovul. Also from Turkic: Ossetian цапуал (capwal, “gallop”), Russian чапаул (čapaul), Persian چپاول (čapâvol).

evidence.head: çarpazlıq
sense_glosses: false relation (a type of dissonance that sometimes occurs in classical polyphonic music, most commonly in vocal music of the Renaissance.)

compound_leaves.head: çarxdiş
compound_leaves.text: Izafet I compound of çarx + diş.

compound_leaves.head: türkəçarə
compound_leaves.text: Compound of türkə (“to a Turk”) + çarə (“remedy”), literally “remedy to a Turk”.

evidence.head: çatlamaq
evidence.text: From çat (“a crack”) + -la. Of onomatopoeic origin, see çırtlamaq. Cognate to Turkish çatlamak.

evidence.head: çatlaq
evidence.text: From çatla + -q. Cognate with Turkish çatlak.

evidence.head: çatlaşmaq
sense_glosses: to chat (to exchange text or voice messages)

compound_leaves.head: ürək çatışmazlığı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of ürək + çatışmazlıq.

evidence.head: naçaq
evidence.text: From Persian ناچاق (nâčâq), from چاق (čâq). Equivalent to na- + çağ.

compound_leaves.head: günün günorta çağı
compound_leaves.text: From gün (“day”) + günorta (“noon, midday”) + çağ (“time, period”), literally “the noon time of the day”.

evidence.head: çağırış
evidence.text: Morphologically, from çağır- (“to call”) + -ış. The military sense is a semantic loan from Russian призы́в (prizýv). The sense 'parliamentary term' is a semantic loan from Russian созы́в (sozýv).

compound_leaves.head: çağırış halı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of çağırış (“call, appeal”) + hal (“case”).

evidence.head: çaşdırmaq
sense_glosses: to confuse, to bewilder, to muddle

evidence.head: çevriliş
sense_glosses: revolution (a sudden, vast change in a situation, a discipline, or the way of thinking and behaving)

compound_leaves.head: çexdilli
compound_leaves.text: From çex + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: çeçendilli
compound_leaves.text: From çeçen (“Chechen”) + dilli.

evidence.head: çeşidlənmə
sense_glosses: verbal noun of çeşidlənmək (“to be sorted”)

evidence.head: çeşidlənmək
sense_glosses: passive of çeşidləmək (“to sort, to assort”)

evidence.head: çimizdirmək
sense_glosses: to bathe (to clean a person by immersion in water or using water)

compound_leaves.head: çimərlik geyimi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of çimərlik (“beach”) + geyimi (“cloth”).

compound_leaves.head: çimərlik paltarı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of çimərlik (“beach”) + paltarı (“cloth”).

compound_leaves.head: meymunçiçəyi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of meymun + çiçək. Literally, "monkey pox".

compound_leaves.head: suçiçəyi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of su + çiçək.

compound_leaves.head: toyuqçiçəyi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of toyuq + çiçək.

evidence.head: çoxluq
evidence.text:
Morphologically çox (“much, many”) + -luq.
The sense 'set' is a semantic loan from Russian мно́жество (mnóžestvo).

compound_leaves.head: alt çoxluq
compound_leaves.text: From alt + çoxluq. Calque of Russian подмно́жество (podmnóžestvo).

compound_leaves.head: çoxallahlı
compound_leaves.text: From çox + allah + -lı.

compound_leaves.head: çoxarvadlı
compound_leaves.text: From çox + arvad + -lı.

compound_leaves.head: çoxatomlu
compound_leaves.text: From çox + atom + -lu.

compound_leaves.head: çoxbucaqlı
compound_leaves.text: Compound of çox (“many”) + bucaqlı (“having (an) angle(s)”).

compound_leaves.head: çoxcildli
compound_leaves.text: From çox + cild + li.

compound_leaves.head: çoxdilli
compound_leaves.text: From çox + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: çoxhecalı
compound_leaves.text: From çox (“many”) + heca (“syllable”) + -lı.

compound_leaves.head: çoxhüceyrəli
compound_leaves.text: From çox (“many”) + hüceyrə (“cell”) + -li.

compound_leaves.head: çoxhədli
compound_leaves.text: From çox + hədd + -li.

compound_leaves.head: çoxmillətli
compound_leaves.text: From çox + millət + -li.

compound_leaves.head: çoxmənalı
compound_leaves.text: From çox + məna + -lı.

compound_leaves.head: çoxmərtəbə
compound_leaves.text: Compound of çox (“many”) + mərtəbə (“floor”).

compound_leaves.head: çoxmərtəbəli
compound_leaves.text: From çox (“many”) + mərtəbə (“floor”) + -li.

compound_leaves.head: çoxnəfərli
compound_leaves.text: From çox (“many”) + nəfər (“person”) + -li.

compound_leaves.head: çoxoyunçulu
compound_leaves.text: From çox (“many”) + oyunçu (“player”) + -lu.

compound_leaves.head: çoxsaylı
compound_leaves.text: From çox + say + -lı, a calque of Russian многочи́сленный (mnogočíslennyj).

compound_leaves.head: çoxsağol
compound_leaves.text: Univerbation of çox (“a lot”) + sağol (“thank you! be at good health!”).

compound_leaves.head: çoxsəslilik
compound_leaves.text: From çox + səs + -li + -lik.

compound_leaves.head: çoxtərəfli
compound_leaves.text: From çox + tərəf + li.

compound_leaves.head: çoxuşaqlı
compound_leaves.text: From çox (“many”) + uşaq (“child”) + -lı.

compound_leaves.head: çoxyerli
compound_leaves.text: From çox (“many”) + yer (“place”) + -li.

evidence.head: çöküntü
sense_glosses: wreckage, debris, rubble, remnant of things that have collapsed

compound_leaves.head: çöl bloku
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of çöl + blok.

compound_leaves.head: çöl eşşəyi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of çöl (“desert”) + eşşək (“donkey”). Calque of Persian گورخر.

compound_leaves.head: çömçəquyruq
compound_leaves.text: Izafet I compound of çömçə + quyruq.

evidence.head: çöpçü
sense_glosses: a folk healer (usually a woman) who is believed to remove small bones or other similar objects stuck in a child’s throat or nose

compound_leaves.head: dişçöpü
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of diş (“tooth”) + çöpü (“straw”).

compound_leaves.head: çörək ağacı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of çörək (“bread”) + ağac (“tree”), Literally, “the tree of bread”.

compound_leaves.head: çörək pulu
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of çörək (“bread”) + pul (“money”)

evidence.head: çözələmək
sense_glosses: to unravel (to clear from complication or difficulty)

evidence.head: çılpaqlıq
evidence.text: Morphologically çılpaq + -lıq. Cognate with Turkish çıplaklık.

evidence.head: çıxarmaq
sense_glosses: to take out, pull out, drag out

evidence.head: çıxarış
sense_glosses: extract (substance extracted from plant or animal tissue)

evidence.head: çıxış
evidence.text:
Morphologically, from çıx- (“to exit”) + -ış.
The sense 'appearance, speech' is a semantic loan from Russian выступле́ние (vystuplénije).
Cognates
Cognate with Turkish çıkış, Crimean Tatar çıqış, Karakhanid [script needed] (čïqïš, “going out, way out, profit”), Kazakh шығыс (šığıs, “exit”), Kyrgyz чыгыш (cıgış, “exit”), Uzbek chiqish (“exit, rising up”), etc.
sense_glosses: output (data sent out of the computer)

compound_leaves.head: hündürəçıxdı
compound_leaves.text: From hündür + -ə + çıx- + -dı.

evidence.head: çəkilmək
sense_glosses: to act, perform in a film

compound_leaves.head: geriçəkilmə
compound_leaves.text: Univerbation of geri + çəkilmə.

compound_leaves.head: yeniçəri
compound_leaves.text: From Ottoman Turkish یڭیچری. Equivalent to yeni + çəri.

evidence.head: çərənləmək
sense_glosses: to babble, to blab, to yap

compound_leaves.head: öd kisəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of öd + kisə. Cognate with Turkish öd kesesi.

evidence.head: ödənişli
sense_glosses: pay, paid, chargeable, to be paid for, requiring payment

evidence.head: öldürmək
evidence.text: Morphologically ölmək (“to die”) + -dür. Cognate with Kazakh өлтіру (öltirüw, “to kill”), Turkish öldürmek (“to kill”), Uzbek o'ldirmoq (“to kill”), Kyrgyz өлтүрүү (öltürüü, “to kill”).

evidence.head: öldürülmə
sense_glosses: verbal noun of öldürülmək (“to be killed”)

evidence.head: ölçü
sense_glosses: criterion measure (a standard against which something can be judged)

compound_leaves.head: eyniölçülü
compound_leaves.text: From eyni (“same”) + ölçülü.

compound_leaves.head: n-ölçülü
compound_leaves.text: From n + ölçülü.

compound_leaves.head: üçölçülü
compound_leaves.text: From üç + ölçülü.

compound_leaves.head: damaqönü
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of damaq + ön. Calque of Russian передненёбный (perednenjóbnyj).

compound_leaves.head: dilönü
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of dil + ön. Calque of Russian переднеязычный (perednejazyčnyj).

evidence.head: öpüşmək
evidence.text: From öpmək (“to kiss”) + -üş. Cognate with Turkish öpüşmek.

compound_leaves.head: ördəkburun
compound_leaves.text: Izafet I compound of ördək (“duck”) + burun (“nose”). Calque of Russian утконо́с (utkonós). Compare Bashkir өйрәкморон (üyräkmurun, “platipus”).

compound_leaves.head: başıörtülü
compound_leaves.text: From baş (“head”) + örtülü (“covered”).

compound_leaves.head: ört-basdır
compound_leaves.text: Imperative compound of ört- (“to cover”) + basdır- (“to bury”). Compare Turkish örtbas.

evidence.head: övladlıq
sense_glosses: the relation between a person and his/her parents
the duties of a person towards his/her parents

evidence.head: özləmək
evidence.text: From öz + -lə. Although the verb is archaic, today it also may be considered a reborrowing if used by speakers influenced by the Turkish language (cf. Turkish özlemek).

evidence.head: özək
evidence.text: A derivation of Proto-Turkic *ȫŕ. By surface analysis, öz + -ək.
sense_glosses: heart (the inner, soft part of a plant stem or root)
inner part (of a machine), core (of an electromagnet)
pulp (the soft center of a tooth)

compound_leaves.head: özbaşına
compound_leaves.text: Compound of öz (“self”) + başına (“head”, third-person singular/plural possessive dative singular). Cognate with Turkmen özbaşyna.

evidence.head: özbaşınalıq
sense_glosses: power abuse; arbitrary will, behaviour or rule

compound_leaves.head: özbəkdilli
compound_leaves.text: From özbək (“Uzbek”) + dilli.

compound_leaves.head: özgələşdirmək
compound_leaves.text: Morphologically özgələş- (“to become alienated”) + dir.

evidence.head: üfüqi
evidence.text: From Arabic أُفُقِيّ (ʔufuqiyy), or from üfüq + -i.

evidence.head: ünsiyyətcil
sense_glosses: sociable (tending to socialize or be social; friendly; inviting; congenial)

compound_leaves.head: ürək çatışmazlığı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of ürək + çatışmazlıq.

compound_leaves.head: ürək-damar
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of ürək + damar.

compound_leaves.head: ürəkbir
compound_leaves.text: From ürək (“heart”) + bir (“one”).

compound_leaves.head: ürəkbulanma
compound_leaves.text: Izafet I compound of ürək + bulanma. Compare Armenian սրտխառնոց (srtxaṙnocʻ, literally “heart-mixedness, heart-confusedness”), Georgian გულისრევა (gulisreva, literally “heart-mixedness, heart-confusedness”).

evidence.head: üstəlik
sense_glosses: besides, at that, in addition; furthermore

compound_leaves.head: axşamüstü
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of axşam + üst.

compound_leaves.head: masaüstü
compound_leaves.text: From masa + üst.

compound_leaves.head: suüstü
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of su + üst.

compound_leaves.head: sözünün üstündə durmaq
compound_leaves.text: söz + üst + durmaq, literally “to stand on a promise”.

compound_leaves.head: yerüstü
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of yer + üst.

compound_leaves.head: üst-baş
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of üst + baş.

compound_leaves.head: üstqurum
compound_leaves.text: From üst + qurum.

compound_leaves.head: üstəgəl
compound_leaves.text: From üstə + gəl, Literally, “come on top of it”

compound_leaves.head: balışüzü
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of balış + üz.

compound_leaves.head: gülərüz
compound_leaves.text: From gülər, a form of gülmək (“to smile”) + üz (“face”).

compound_leaves.head: ikiüzlü
compound_leaves.text: From iki (“two”) + üz (“face”) + -lü.

compound_leaves.head: üz-göz
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of üz + göz.

compound_leaves.head: üzügülər
compound_leaves.text: From üz + gülər.

compound_leaves.head: üzüqara
compound_leaves.text: From üz (“face”) + qara (“black”).

evidence.head: üzrlü
sense_glosses: having a valid reason, having a valid cause

compound_leaves.head: cümlə üzvü
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of cümlə (“sentence”) + üzv (“member”), Russian член предложе́ния (člen predložénija).

compound_leaves.head: bilərzik
compound_leaves.text: From Old Turkic [script needed] (bilezük, bilerzük, bilersük), composed of bilək (“wrist”) + üzük (“ring”).

evidence.head: üçüncü
evidence.text: Morphologically üç + -üncü. Cognate with Kazakh үшінші (üšinši), Old Turkic 𐰇𐰲𐰨 (üčünč), Turkish üçüncü, Turkmen üçünji.

evidence.head: üçəm
sense_glosses: One of or a group of three siblings born at the same time to the same mother
A traditional gambling game played with knucklebones
A ewe or goat that has birthed three offspring at once.

compound_leaves.head: muğam üçlüyü
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of muğam (“mugham”) + üçlüyü (“trio”).

compound_leaves.head: üçbucaq
compound_leaves.text: Compound of üç + bucaq.

compound_leaves.head: üçvahidlik
compound_leaves.text: üç + vahidlik.

compound_leaves.head: üçölçülü
compound_leaves.text: From üç + ölçülü.

compound_leaves.head: üçüzlü
compound_leaves.text: Compound of üç (“three”) + üzlü (“having (an) edge(s)”).

evidence.head: üşütmək
sense_glosses: to chill, to cool, to hit with (unpleasant) cool
to let catch a cold, to let catch a chill; to expose to cold so that someone catches a cold

evidence.head: şabalıdı
sense_glosses: chestnut (a dark, reddish-brown colour, as seen on the fruit of the chestnut tree)

compound_leaves.head: şadlıq evi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of şadlıq + ev.

evidence.head: şadaralamaq
sense_glosses: to riddle (put something through a riddle or sieve; to sieve; to sift)

compound_leaves.head: ətirşah
compound_leaves.text: Izafet I compound of ətir + şah.

evidence.head: şanslı
evidence.text: From şans + lı. The sense 'lucky' is a semantic loan from Turkish şanslı.

compound_leaves.head: şeş-beş
compound_leaves.text: From şeş (“six”) + beş (“five”).

compound_leaves.head: şirin pambıq
compound_leaves.text: From şirin + pambıq. Literally, “sweet cotton”.

compound_leaves.head: şirinquş
compound_leaves.text: Univerbation of şirin (“sweet”) + quş (“bird”).

compound_leaves.head: vətənşivən
compound_leaves.text: Blend of vətənpərvər (“patriot”) + şivən (“weeping”).

compound_leaves.head: şorqoğalı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of şor (“salty”) + qoğalı (“bun”).

evidence.head: ştanqçı
evidence.text: From ştanq + -çı. Calque of Russian штанги́ст (štangíst).

evidence.head: şumlamaq
sense_glosses: to till (to plow in preparation for sowing)

evidence.head: şöhrətpərəst
sense_glosses: vainglorious, having excessive ambition for renown

compound_leaves.head: şəfqət bacısı
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of şəfqət + bacı

compound_leaves.head: şəhlagöz
compound_leaves.text: From şəhla + göz.

evidence.head: həmşəhər
sense_glosses: someone from the same town or city

compound_leaves.head: şəhərlərarası
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of şəhərlər + ara.

compound_leaves.head: şəhərsalma
compound_leaves.text: From şəhər + sal- + -ma.

compound_leaves.head: badamşəkilli
compound_leaves.text: From badam (“almond”) + şəkil (“shape”) + -li.

compound_leaves.head: narşərab
compound_leaves.text: Izafet I compound of nar (“pomegranate”) + şərab (“wine”).

evidence.head: şərbətçi
sense_glosses: a person who makes and sells sherbet

compound_leaves.head: şəxsiyyət vəsiqəsi
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of şəxsiyyət + vəsiqə.

evidence.head: əclaflıq
sense_glosses: disgrace, meanness, a despicable act, vileness

compound_leaves.head: haqq-ədalət
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of haqq (“truth, right”) + ədalət (“justice”).

compound_leaves.head: kitab əhli
compound_leaves.text: Izafet II compound of kitab + əhl. Calque of Arabic أَهْل الْكِتَاب (ʔahl al-kitāb).

evidence.head: əhvalat
sense_glosses: account (a record of events; a relation or narrative)

compound_leaves.head: əhval-ruhiyyə
compound_leaves.text: Dvandva compound of əhval (“mood”) + ruhiyyə (“spirits”).

evidence.head: əkinçi
evidence.text: Morphologically from əkin (“plantation”) + -çi. Compare Turkish akıncı, Northern Kurdish akincî.

compound_leaves.head: əkinəyararlı
compound_leaves.text: Univerbation of əkinə + yararlı.

compound_leaves.head: əkinəyararsız
compound_leaves.text: Univerbation of əkinə + yararsız.

evidence.head: əlləmək
sense_glosses: to handle, to touch; to feel with the hand; to grope
to beckon (To wave or nod to somebody with the intention to make the person come closer)

evidence.head: əlləşmək
sense_glosses: to struggle, have difficulty with something, to work hard to solve or repair something

evidence.head: arxac
evidence.text:

Cognate with the synonymous dialectal Turkish arkaç, argaç, arhaç, arḫaç.
sense_glosses: resting place for sheep or cattle out in the free during herding in the summer

evidence.head: azarkeş
evidence.text:
A semantic parallel or a calque of Russian боле́льщик (bolélʹščik, “one who is ill with, i.e. obsessed with something”) created by suffixing azar (“illness”) + -keş. The lexical component of the calque is probably not transparent to the speakers anymore (if ever?), which is evidenced by the frequent variant azərkeş. Not attested in a dictionary from 1941, but appears in more recent dictionaries. Russian боле́льщик (bolélʹščik) is attested since 1948.
Compare also xəstə (“sick, ill → fan, buff, devotee”), as in futbol xəstəsi 'football fan', meyxana xəstəsi 'meykhana buff'.

evidence.head: badalaq
evidence.text: Per Bəşirov, comes from earlier *badaqlaq with the drop of q. By surface analysis, from badaq (“hobble, spancel”) + -laq. Perhaps, a semantic development, exhibiting an extension of specific devices' meanings into the more general trip sense. The general sense is thought to have influenced the original badaq itself, as its first definition is described as synonymous to badalaq with the further list of specifics in the ADIL. Cognate to Turkish badalak, badalak vurmak. See more at badaq.

evidence.head: kürtük

From *kürt (“snow drift”), equivalent to *kürt- + -ük. Related to Yakut күрт- (kürt-, “to shovel”), Karakhanid [script needed] (küri-), Karakhanid [script needed] (kürä-, “to scoop, shovel”). See also көрәк (küräk, “shovel”).

Tatar көрт (kört, “snow drift”),
Kumyk кюрт (kürt, “snow drift”),
Southern Altai күрт (“snow drift”),
Shor кӧрт (“snow drift”);
also
Kazakh күртік (kürtik, “snow drift”),
Kyrgyz күртүк (kürtük)/күрткү (kürtkü, “snow drift”),
Khakas кӧртік (körtìk, “snow drift”).

evidence.head: kürtük
evidence.text:
From *kürt (“snow drift”), equivalent to *kürt- + -ük. Related to Yakut күрт- (kürt-, “to shovel”), Karakhanid [script needed] (küri-), Karakhanid [script needed] (kürä-, “to scoop, shovel”). See also көрәк (küräk, “shovel”).
Compare to
Tatar көрт (kört, “snow drift”),
Kumyk кюрт (kürt, “snow drift”),
Southern Altai күрт (“snow drift”),
Shor кӧрт (“snow drift”);
also
Kazakh күртік (kürtik, “snow drift”),
Kyrgyz күртүк (kürtük)/күрткү (kürtkü, “snow drift”),
Khakas кӧртік (körtìk, “snow drift”).
